description.en: The partition is a barrier that prevents the supernal light from radiating into lower [levels](/topics/level) of existence. As a result, the partition rebuffs it, like a mirror that reflects light back to its source. The partition is manifest during the process of creation, as a result of the first [constriction](/topics/constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)), and it is a way of describing the resistance of the created being to receiving the supernal light in its fourth [level](/topics/level), which corresponds to, and is called, [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). The collision between the supernal light and the partition causes the light to be rebuffed, and as a result, the [returning light](/topics/returning-light1) becomes a new vessel for the supernal light. There are partitions at every [level](/topics/level) of reality, and each partition has different degrees of [opacity](/topics/opacity) ([*ovyut*](/topics/ovyut)) and [hardness](/topics/kashyut) ([*kashyut*](/topics/kashyut)), giving rise to a variance in the structures of [returning light](/topics/returning-light1) that a given partition generates. This also underlies the variance found in the different [levels](/topics/level) of reality, such as the [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf). In addition to the partitions that rebuff the light, there are partitions that serve as a terminating point of a particular [level](/topics/level) of existence (such as a [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1)), and the division between one [level](/topics/level) of existence and another. In general terms, it can be said that the different operations of these differences in the partitions are the causes of the differences between the various [levels](/topics/level) and stages of creation, as a result of the variance of [opacity](/topics/opacity) and [hardness](/topics/kashyut) and the resulting varying heights of [returning light](/topics/returning-light1).

While there are a few pharaohs mentioned in the Tanakh, the most famous one was the Pharaoh who enslaved the Israelites and hardened his heart in his refusal to set them free. During his reign, God struck Egypt with ten plagues. Pharaoh and his army were destroyed when they chased the fleeing Israelites into the Red Sea.
description.he: במקרא מוזכרים כמה פרעונים, אך הידוע בהם הוא פרעה ששעבד את בני ישראל במצרים והקשה את ליבו כאשר נדרש לשחררם. בתקופת שלטונו הִכה האל את מצרים בעשר מכות. פרעה וחילו טובעו בים סוף לאחר שהחליטו לרדוף אחרי העם הבורח ממצרים.

description.en: R. Yoshiah was a student of R. Yishmael and was often involved in disputes with R. Yonatan. It appears that he left Israel during the time of the Hadrianic persecutions, as we read about teaching at the academy of R. Yehudah b. Betirah in northern Babylonia..
description.he: רבי יאשיה היה תלמידו של רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע ולעיתים קרובות מוזכר במחלוקות עם רבי יונתן. מאחר שהוא מוזכר מלמד בישיבה של רבי יהודה בן בתירא בצפון בבל, משוער שעזב את ארץ ישראל בתקופת רדיפות אדריאנוס.

description.en: A tzaddik is someone who embodies tzedek, or righteousness, in order to overcome their surroundings in order to serve as a source of inspiration and spiritual help for others. In Hasidic literature, the tzaddik often pleads with God on behalf of the Jewish people.
description.he: המילה צדיק גזורה מהמילה "צדק". צדיק הוא אדם המגלם בתוכו רמה יוצאת דופן של צדק ויושרה ובאופן זה משמש מקור השראה וסיוע רוחני לאחרים. בספרות החסידית פעמים רבות הצדיק מתחנן לאלוהים בשם העם היהודי.

description.en: Education is a value discussed throughout the Jewish textual tradition. Various biblical narratives demonstrate the significance of transmitting values to the next generation. Rabbinic sources analyze the parental obligation to educate one's children, as well as the development of communal educational frameworks.
description.he: חינוך הוא ערך הנידון לאורך ספרות המסורת היהודית. סיפורים מקראיים שונים מדגימים את החשיבות של העברת ערכים לדור הבא. מקורות רבניים מנתחים את חובת ההורים לחנך את ילדיהם, כמו גם את פיתוחן של מסגרות חינוך קהילתיות.

description.en: Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, also known as the Sabbath of Sabbaths, is considered by many to be the holiest day of the Jewish year. Traditionally, the day is one of  fasting and prayer for a clean slate at the start of the new year.
description.he:
יום הכיפורים (מכונה גם ״שבת שבתון״) חל בעשרה בתשרי.  
על פי המסורת היהודית זהו היום הקדוש ביותר בשנה. על פי התורה יש לענות את הנפש ולא לעשות מלאכה.  חכמים הגדירו את העינוי כצום לצד דברים נוספים, והתפילות עוסקות בבקשת סליחה ובתשובה.

description.en: Rabbi Shimon b. Pazzi, who was also known as Rabbi Simon, was a student of Rabbi Yehoshua b. Levi and among his students was Rav Hilkiyah. He was the father or R. Yehudah b. Pazzi.

description.en: The second of the *sefirot*, following *Keter*, this *sefira* is characterized by the essence of giving and bestowal from the Creator to the created beings – or, in other words, the first [level](/topics/level) or phase of the supernal light, or direct light, that emanates from the essence of the Creator, which is characterized by the will to give and is also called the “light of wisdom” (each of the five main [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are often described as [levels](/topics/level), with [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) serving as the “root” [level](/topics/level) (the zero point) and the next four [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) representing [levels](/topics/level) one through four). It is called *Ḥokhma*, or Wisdom, because it emanates all the wisdoms in existence. Additionally, it represents the concept of the unbounded mind and intellect, undefined and unrestricted, of the as yet undefined first flash of awareness.  This *sefira* is present at the [head](/topics/head2) of every [level](/topics/level) and [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1). Each of the five primary *sefirot* is parallel to one of the five worlds that form existence. The parallel world to this *sefira* is the world of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) which is united with the Creator and has no limitations or boundaries. Each of the five primary *sefirot* is also parallel to one of the five [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf). The [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) that is parallel to this [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) is called *Abba*, or “Father.”  Certain lower [levels](/topics/level) of existence are also referred to as the *sefira* of *Ḥokhma*. This is because they all share a basic characteristic: They are all derivatives of the first [level](/topics/level) of the supernal light, or the light of wisdom.

Blessing is the act of calling down God's favor upon someone or something. The one calling down the blessing can be a person, an angel, or God Godself. Blessings are meant to bring benefits to their recipient, such as material goods or having many offspring. Tradition recognizes a four-part typology of liturgical blessings: on performing a commandment; in prayer; on partaking of sustenance; and in praise of God.
description.he: ברכה היא קריאה להשראת החסד האלוקי על אדם או על דבר מסוים. המברך יכול להיות אדם, מלאך או הקב"ה עצמו. ברכות נועדו להיטיב עם המתברך, כדוגמת ברכה לשפע חומרי או לצאצאים רבים.

description.en: *Bina* is the third of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot), following the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). It is the second [level](/topics/level) of the supernal light, or direct light, that emanates from the essence of the Creator. This second [level](/topics/level) or phase represents the desire of the created being to give and bestow and is therefore called the light of giving, as a continuation of the light of the Creator, the light of wisdom. It is called *Bina* or Understanding, because from it flows forth the power of understanding, of apprehending one thing for another. *Bina* is also a reference to different lower [levels](/topics/level) or *sefirot* in the structure of reality that are derivatives of the second [level](/topics/level) of the direct light.  *Bina* is considered a “female” (or receiving) *sefira*, because it receives the light of wisdom. Additionally, at the root of *Bina* lies the yearning of the created beings that represents the will to receive that is embedded in existence. From a different perspective, *Bina* is found in of the [head](/topics/head2) of the [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) constructs, that is in the mind, so to speak, which includes the first three [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), and *Bina*.  Each of the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) is parallel to one of the five worlds that form existence. The world that is parallel to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Bina* is the world of [*Beria*](/topics/beria1). Each of the five primary *sefirot* is also parallel to one of the five [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf). The [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) that is parallel to *Bina* is called *Imma*, or “Mother.” Like a mother, *Bina* contains the roots of the *sefirot* that emanate from it, [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) with its [*six extremities*](/topics/six-extremities) and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). Additionally, the second [constriction](/topics/constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)) that forms the backdrop for the [*world of tikkun](/topics/world-of-tikkun) ([rectification](/topics/world-of-tikkun))*, takes place within the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Bina*.

Marriage is an institution and value discussed throughout Jewish sources, which tell stories of Jewish marriages, analyze the multitude of legal aspects involved in marriage ceremonies, and consider the broader significance of this unique union between two souls.
description.he: מוסד הנישואים מבסס ומקדש את חיי המשפחה והזוגיות ביהדות. הנישואים הם ערך שנידון בהרחבה במקורות רבים בהם מופיעים סיפורים על נישואים, ניתוח של ההיבטים ההלכתיים הכרוכים בטקס הנישואים ובחיי הנישואים, וגם פרישה של הגות ומחשבה בה מופיעה המשמעות העמוקה של איחוד בין שתי נשמות.

image_caption.he: חתונה יהודית, א. טרנקובסקי (פולין, 1875-1900). אוסף מוזיאון מאגנס

description.en: Torah study involves the study of sacred Jewish texts, like the Torah, Mishnah, Talmud, and works of midrash, kabbalah, and Jewish thought. It is considered central to religious practice, with blessings acknowledging the commandment to engage in Torah study and thanking God for giving the Torah featured at the beginning of daily liturgy. The subject, form, and nature of Torah study vary between individuals and communities.
description.he: לימוד תורה הוא חלק אינטגרלי מהמסורת היהודית. הוא כרוך בלימוד הטקסטים היהודיים, לרבות תנ״ך, משנה, תלמוד, ספרי קבלה ומחשבת ישראל, ועוד. לימוד התורה נחשב למצווה ומוערך מאוד בתרבות היהודית כאמצעי לחיבור עם האל, להעמקת הידע וההבנה של האדם ולשיפור התנהגותו המוסרית והאתית. מקור המצווה  הוא במספר פסוקים בספר דברים: ״וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם לְדַבֵּר בָּם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ (דברים, יא, יט), ״וּלְמַדְתֶּם אֹתָם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם לַעֲשֹׂתָם״ (דברים, ה, א), ״וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם״ (דברים, ו, ז).

image_caption.he: שמואל הירשנברג, בית ספר לתלמוד 1887,  המוזאון הלאומי בקראקוב

titles.text: The Lord and the Jewish People

description.en: R. Chiyya's two sons, Yehudah b. Chiyya and Chizkiyah b. Chiyya, came with him from Babylonia to Palestine as young adults. Already known for their scholarship, they added distinction to Rabbi's academy. They died prematurely and were buried on either side of their father.
description.he: שני בניו של רבי חייא באו איתו מבבל לארץ ישראל כנערים. הואיל וכבר נודעו בחוכמתם בתורה, הוסיפו כבוד לבית מדרשו של רבי. מתו בגיל צעיר ונקברו משני צידיו של אביהם.

description.en: R. Levi lived during the time of R. Yochanan. At first unnoticed, he became a regular speaker at R. Yochanan's academy and regaled its scholars with profound textual interpretations.
description.he: רבי לוי חי בתקופתו של רבי יוחנן. בתחילה לא זכה לתשומת לב רבה, אך בחלוף הזמן היה לדובר קבוע בבית מדרשו של רבי יוחנן והדהים את התלמידים בדרשותיו העמוקות.

description.en: Hezekiah was the king of Judah who went on a religious campaign of reform to shore up Israelite monotheism. He prepared Jerusalem for an Assyrian siege that it withstood thanks to both miracles and his construction of a water tunnel to bring water into the city.
description.he: חזקיהו הוא ממלכי יהודה שהנהיג רפורמה דתית שמטרתה ביסוס המונותאיזם הישראלי. הוא חיזק את ירושלים לקראת מצור אשורי, והעיר ניצלה בזכות שילוב של השגחת האל עם המפעל המרשים של חזקיהו: חציבת נקבת השילוח שהבטיחה אספקת מים לעיר במהלך המצור.

image_caption.en: The Pool of Hezekiah, Jerusalem. 1890. Library of Congress
image_caption.he: בריכת חזקיה, 1890. Library of Congress

description.en: The *sefirot* represent ten ways through which the Creator reveals Himself in the creation, with each *sefira* representing a different degree of revelation. The term *sefira* itself has the same root as the word sapir, which means sapphire or radiance, indicating that the divine light is contained within the *sefirot* and illuminates the creation through them.  Generally, there are ten *sefirot*: [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). But in essence there are five primary *sefirot*: [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). Additionally, each of these five *sefirot* are themselves composed of the other *sefirot*, since everything in reality is formed out of *sefirot*. Thus, for example, the *sefira* of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) contains the [*levels*](/topics/level) of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1).  As for the five remaining *sefirot*, [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), and [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), they are encompassed within the *sefira* of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). Like the other *sefirot*, the *sefira* of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) contains all five *sefirot*, but in this case they are called by different names: In this context, they are called [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah) and [*Hod*](/topics/hod1). The reason the sefirot are given different names is that a different kind of light from that of the other *sefirot*, called the “light of giving,” is revealed through [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). Although they are named differently, they are still, in a sense, the same five *sefirot* mentioned above. Thus, [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed) is referred to as the [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura) as the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah) as the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Hod*](/topics/hod1) as the [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). In addition to these five, there is another *sefira* that incorporates all the [*levels*](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) called [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1).

Mordekhai is one of the protagonists of the [book of Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/Esther?tab=contents). A courtier to the king, he saved the king from an assassination attempt and helped his cousin [Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/esther?tab=sources) to save the Jewish people from genocide.
description.he: מרדכי הוא מגיבורי מגילת אסתר. הוא היה מחצרני המלך אחשוורוש, הציל את המלך מניסיון רצח וסייע לבת דודו אסתר להציל את העם היהודי מכליה.

description.en: Leadership is a concept that features throughout the Jewish textual tradition. Biblical stories of leaders like the matriarchs and patriarchs, Moses, and Joshua, offer much material for leadership analysis. Rabbinic sources throughout the ages debate the merits of different models of leadership, and contemporary authors grapple with how to approach leadership today in light of ancient texts.

image_caption.en: Issachar Ber Ryback - Interior with red carpet (1917)
image_caption.he: יששכר בר ריבק  - פנים עם שטיח אדום (1917)

description.en: As the head of the Sanhedrin (the Jewish court), Shammai served as Hillel’s colleague, as well as his intellectual rival. He studied under Avtalyon and Shemaya and was a pious and punctilious defender of the tradition. His many students were known to be even sharper than those of Hillel.
description.he: שמאי שימש כאב בית הדין בצד הלל הנשיא והיה גם בר-פלוגתא שלו. למד עם שמעיה ואבטליון וגונן באדיקות ובדייקנות על המסורת. תלמידיו הרבים נודעו בחדותם בשנינותם, שגברה על תלמידי הלל.

image_caption.he: Hanukkah Lamp, Eastern Germany, Bohemia/Moravia, or Austrian Empire, mid 18th century

description.en: Summakhos was a devoted and gifted student of R. Meir. Besides his knowledge of Jewish law, he was known for his command of Greek.
description.he: סוּמָכוֹס היה תלמיד מסור ומחונן של רבי מאיר. מלבד בקיאותו בהלכה, נודע בשליטתו בשפה היוונית.

description.en: The opening two [chapters](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.1.1?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=he) of the Torah describe how God created the world in six days and rested on the seventh. These chapters are some of the most analyzed words in the Jewish textual tradition and serve as a basis for discussions of topics like [human dignity](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/human-dignity?tab=admin), God's role in the world, Shabbat, and humankind's responsibility for continuing the creation process and caring for the world.

Sarah is the mother of the Jewish people and the wife of [Abraham](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/abraham?tab=sources). After a long struggle with infertility, she bore a child in her old age, [Isaac](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/isaac?tab=sources).
description.he: שרה היא דמות מקראית המופיעה בספר בראשית. היא הראשונה מבין 'ארבע האמהות' והיתה אשת אברהם. לאחר התמודדות עם עקרות ממושכת זכתה בזקנתה לבן יחיד, יצחק.

image_caption.en: Sarah. 1972 stamps of Israel, Abel Pann
image_caption.he: שרה.  1972, בולי אמנות ישראלית - אבל פן

description.en: Jewish circumcision dates back to the book of Genesis, in which God instructs Abraham to circumcise himself and the males of his household as a marker of the covenant between God and God's people. God also instructs that Abraham's future descendants circumcise male babies at the age of eight days, a practice Jews have observed through the generations.
description.he: ברית מילה היא מצווה יסודית מהתורה לפיה יש למול את עורלת הזכרים  ביום השמיני ללידתם. מצווה זו מכונה "בריתו של אברהם אבינו" מפני שהראשון שצווה בה וקיים אותה הוא אברהם. מי שלא נימול לאחר לידתו חייב במילת עצמו וכך גם לגבי מי שעובר תהליך של גיור. במהלך טקס הברית מעניקים לתינוק את שמו. הברית נערכת בדרך כלל על ידי מוהל באירוע חגיגי המלווה  בסעודת מצווה.

image_caption.en: A child being circumcised, Hebrew Mss 1687. Wellcome Collection.
image_caption.he: ברית מילה, כתב יד עברי 1687, אוסף וולקאם

description.en: Haman is the villain of the [book of Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/Esther). A vizier of King [Ahasuerus](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/ahasuerus?sort=Relevance&), he planned a genocide against the Jewish people, but his plans were thwarted by [Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/esther) and her uncle, [Mordekhai](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mordekhai?tab=sources). As a descendant of the nation of [Amalek](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/amalek?tab=sources), the first nation to attack the Israelites soon after they left Egypt, Haman comes from a long line of enemies of the Jewish people.
description.he: המן הוא הרשע במגילת אסתר והבכיר בין שרי המלך אחשוורוש. הוא תכנן לבצע רצח עם שבו יושמדו היהודים בכל מדינות המלך אחשוורוש. תוכניתו סוכלה על ידי מרדכי ואסתר.

image_caption.en: Ahasveros and Haman at the Feast of Esther, Rembrandt, 1660
image_caption.he: אחשוורוש והמן במשתה אסתר, רמברנדט, 1660

description.en: The lights of the [head](/topics/head2) are called brains (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 8, Q & A 32).

Miriam was a prophetess who, along with her brothers, [Moses](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/moses?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) and [Aaron](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/aaron?tab=sources), led the Israelites out of Egypt. She led the Jewish women in song and dance. According to midrashic stories, a well of fresh water followed the Israelites in the desert in her merit and disappeared upon her death.
description.he: מרים היא נביאה מקראית, ויחד עם אחיה משה ואהרן הנהיגה את בני ישראל בדרכם במדבר. היא הובילה את הנשים בשיר ובריקוד אחרי קריעת ים סוף. על פי המדרש, בזכותה ליוותה באר מים חיים את בני ישראל במסעותיהם במדבר, והבאר שקעה ונעלמה עם מותה.

image_caption.en: Miriam Watching the Finding of Moses in the Bulrushes, Simeon Solomon, 1859, From the Robert Isaacson Collection, Gift of James David Draper, 2002, The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
image_caption.he: מרים צופה במציאת משה בסוף, שמעון סולומון, 1859, מאוסף רוברט אייזקסון, מתנת ג'יימס דייוויד דרייפר, 2002, מוזיאון המטרופוליטן.

description.en: Jeremiah is one of the major Jewish prophets. He warned of the coming destruction of Jerusalem by Babylon as punishment for the sins of Israel but was mocked and ignored. After the destruction of the First Temple and Jerusalem in 586 BCE, he went into exile alongside many other Judeans. The books of Jeremiah and Lamentations are traditionally attributed to him.
description.he: ירמיהו הוא אחד הנביאים הבולטים במקרא. הוא הזהיר את העם שירושלים תיחרב על ידי הבבלים כעונש על חטאי עם ישראל, אך העם לעג לו והתעלם מדבריו. עם חורבן ירושלים גלה ירמיהו לבבל עם רבים מבני יהודה. מקובל לייחס לו את כתיבת ספר ירמיהו וספר איכה.

image_caption.en: Jeremiah, Ephraim Moses Lilien
image_caption.he: ירמיהו, אפרים משה ליליאן

description.en: Rav Matenah was a student of Shmuel and became an expert in the decisions of his teacher, together with Rav Matenah's contemporary, Rav Yehudah. He was the rabbi in the town of Paphunya, near Pumbedita.
description.he: רב מתנה היה תלמיד של שמואל עד שנעשה, יחד עם בן דורו רב יהודה, מומחה לפסיקותיו של רבו. היה רבה של העיר פאפוניא הסמוכה לפומבדיתא.

description.en: The Mishkan (in English, Tabernacle) was the temporary, portable Temple that the Jews were commanded to build after the revelation at [Mount Sinai](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mount-sinai?tab=sources). It had all of the furnishings of the future Temple and served the same functions, but it was smaller and used fabrics and animal skins for its walls and roof.
description.he: המשכן היה המקדש הנייד והזמני שבני ישראל הצטוו לבנות אחרי ההתגלות בהר סיני. המשכן והמקדש מילאו את אותו התפקיד וכן שימשו בהם אותם הכלים, אך המשכן היה קטן יותר וקירותיו וגגו היו עשויים עורות ובדים.

image_caption.en: A sacrifice taking place in the tabernacle in the wilderness; the encampments of the Jewish tribes spread out to the horizon. Coloured lithograph. Wellcome Collection.
image_caption.he: קורבן במשכן במדבר; המחנות של שבטי ישראל מתפשטים עד לאופק. ליתוגרפיה צבעונית. מקור: אוסף ולקאם.

description.en: Balaam is a non-Israelite biblical prophet whose story appears in the book of Numbers. As the Israelites are wandering in the desert, the Moabite King Balak pays him to curse the Israelites. Balaam, however, is only able to speak the words that God puts in his mouth and ends up blessing the Israelites instead.
description.he: בלעם בן בעור הוא נביא מקראי שאינו מבני ישראל. בשעת נדודי בני ישראל במדבר שילם לו בלק מלך מואב שיקלל את בני ישראל. הוא הצליח להוציא מפיו רק את המילים שהאל שם בפיו, וכך בסופו של דבר בירך את עם ישראל במקום לקללו.

image_caption.en: Bala'am and his Donkey, Ephraim Moses Lilien. Before 1925.
image_caption.he: בלעם והאתון, אפרים משה ליליאן. לפני 1925

description.en: Chanukkah is an eight-day winter holiday commemorating the Jewish victory over the Seleucid Greek oppressors in 164 BCE. It is widely known as the "Festival of Lights" due to the practice of lighting a candle or oil lamp each night of the holiday. This ritual recalls the miracle of the oil, in which a small container of oil for the Temple menorah lasted for eight nights, after it was expected to last for only one.
description.he: חג החנוכה הוא חג בן שמונה ימים החל בחודש כסלו בחודשי החורף, לזכר נצחון היהודים על היוונים במאה שנייה לפני הספירה. הוא מוכר כ"חג האור" משום שמדליקים בו נרות בכל ימות החג. הדלקת הנרות מזכירה את הנס שבו השמן במנורת המקדש הספיק לשמונה לילות - למרות שהיה אמור להספיק רק ללילה אחד.

description.en: Ezra was a priest who, when the Persians conquered the Babylonian empire and allowed the Jews to return, led the Jews to Israel and in rebuilding the Temple. He instituted a series of reforms meant to bring the Jewish people back to their religion.
description.he: עזרא הוא כוהן בתקופת שיבת ציון. אחרי כיבוש בבל על ידי הפרסים, התיר כורש מלך פרס ליהודים לשוב לארץ ישראל ולבנות מחדש את בית המקדש. עזרא עמד בראשם והנהיג סדרה של רפורמות שנועדה להשיב את היהודים למסורת הדתית שלהם.

description.en: In Judaism, priests are believed to be the descendants of [Aaron](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/aaron?tab=sources). In the Bible, they are charged with doing the ritual work in the [Mishkan](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) and later the Temples, under the leadership of a [high priest](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/high-priest?tab=sources). In Temple times, priests were also entitled to certain gifts and portions of sacrifices. Today, some people of priestly descent recite a special blessing in the synagogue and are careful to avoid contact with corpses, among other responsibilities and restrictions. The Hebrew word for priest is kohen.

description.en: Benjamin was the youngest son of Jacob. His mother Rachel died giving birth to him. He was especially beloved of Jacob and when he and his brothers traveled to Egypt to ask for food, Joseph accused Benjamin of stealing from him. Benjamin's brothers defended him, showing that they'd changed and grown.
description.he: בנימין הוא הצעיר בבני יעקב, בן זקונים לאביו. אימו רחל מתה בלידתו. הוא היה אהוב במיוחד על יעקב. כאשר נסע עם אֶחיו למצרים לבקש אוכל, יוסף, שהיה המשנה למלך מצרים, האשים אותו בגנבה. יתר אחיו הגנו עליו בהפגנת נאמנות שהעידה על שינוי בגישתם כלפי בני רחל.

description.en: Sukkot is a weeklong celebration of the harvest in early fall. It is celebrated by the building of temporary booths — that is, sukkot — outside homes in which people eat their meals and sometimes even sleep. The booths are reminders of the transience of life and the sheltering presence of God.
description.he: חג הסוכות, הוא חג האסיף, נמשך שבעה ימים ומצוין בחודש תשרי על-ידי בניית סוכה מחוץ לבית, בה  אוכלים וחלק גם ישנים. הסוכה היא תזכורת לסוכות שבנו בני ישראל ביציאת מצרים, ומסמלת את ארעיות החיים ואת נוכחותו המגוננת של ה'

Pinchas was a priest best known for his violent reaction to Israelite worship of the god Ba'al Pe'or. As this worship was associated with sexual relationships between Israelite men and Moabite and Midianite women, he killed one such couple mid-intercourse. Pinchas was a leader of the Israelites when they went into the Promised Land.
description.he: פינחס נודע בעיקר בשל תגובתו האלימה נגד המשתחווים לבעל פעור. פולחן בעל פעור היה כרוך במגע מיני בין גברים מבני ישראל ונשים מואביות ומדייניות, ופינחס הרג זוג כזה בשעת מעשה. הוא היה מבכירי ההנהגה של עם ישראל בכניסתם לארץ המובטחת.

description.en: Rav Chiya b.Ashi was a student of Rav and was his personal assistant. Hence he was able to pass on many accounts of Rav's practices, which were used as legal precedents.

enBio.value: Rabbi Yehuda Ashlag, also known as the Ba’al HaSulam, was a rabbi and kabbalist. Born in Poland, he emigrated to Israel in 1921 and was appointed rabbi of Givat Shaul, Jerusalem. He is best known for his work Talmud Eser Sefirot, a commentary on the work of Isaac Luria, as well as HaSulam, a commentary on the Zohar. While kabbalah was traditionally treated as a body of secrets reserved for elite students, Ashlag believed it held the keys to finding meaning and achieving personal and social reform, and should be made accessible to all. He and his students were instrumental in the contemporary popularization of kabbalah study.

description.en: R. Yishmael b. Yose studied under his father, R. Yose b. Chalafta, and most of his many teachings are stated in the name of his father. He was a friend and study partner of R. Yehudah haNasi. At one point, he controversially worked for the Roman government catching thieves.
description.he: רבי ישמעאל למד אצל אביו, רבי יוסי בן חלפתא, ורוב האמרות שלו מובאות בשם אביו. למד עם רבי יהודה הנשיא. בתקופה מסוימת פעל באופן שנוי במחלקות כשסייע לשלטון הרומאי בלכידת גנבים.
המואבים הם צאצאי לוט, והתורה מצווה על בני ישראל לא לתקוף אותם אך גם לא להטמיע אותם בהם. דוד המלך הוא צאצא של מואבייה שהתגיירה – רות. ממלכת מואב שכנה בירדן של ימינו.
description.en: Moab’s residents were descended from Lot, and the Torah commands the Israelites to neither attack nor absorb the Moabites. Notably, King David is descended from a Moabite, the convert Ruth. Moab was located in modern-day Jordan.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Tiferet* is the sixth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), *Tiferet*, and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) –*Tiferet* is parallel to the third [level](/topics/level) of the direct light of giving emanating from the Creator. This [level](/topics/level) of light is primarily drawn from the desire of the created beings to bond with the Creator, a will to give, but it also contains a certain amount of the will to receive the light of the Creator, which draws in illuminations from the light of wisdom.  *Tiferet* means “Beauty” (the concept of harmony), and it is called by this name because it is able to integrate both kinds of light within it, the light of wisdom, and the light of giving. This integration, which can be thought of as being formed of two columns of light, as well as an intermediating column which connects them, is the harmonious beauty of this *sefira*. It is this integrative capacity and its unique combination of lights that gives *Tiferet* its unique characterization in which the five *sefirot* that comprise it are given different names (recall that each *sefira* is formed of all five *sefirot*): The [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) in *Tiferet* is called [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed). The [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) in *Tiferet* is called [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura). The [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) in *Tiferet* is called *Tiferet*. The *Tiferet* within *Tiferet* is called *Netzaḥ*. The [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) within *Tiferet* is called [*Hod*](/topics/hod1). In addition to these five, there is a sixth [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) in *Tiferet* called [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), which includes the preceding five within it. It is this grouping of the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) that gives rise to the familiar count of ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot).  In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), *Tiferet* is considered the [body](/topics/body3) of the [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1). Two hands ([*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed) and [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura)) emerge from the [body](/topics/body3), as well as two legs ([*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah) and [*Hod*](/topics/hod1)) and the limb of procreation and life ([*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1)), thus forming the image of the human body. The [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) that correlates to *Tiferet* is [*Ze’er Anpin*](/topics/zeer-anpin1), which encompasses the [*six extremities*](/topics/six-extremities). Each of the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) is also parallel to one of the five worlds that form existence. The world that correlates to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Tiferet* is the world of [*Yetzira*](/topics/yetzira1).
description.he: ​​ספירת התפארת היא הספירה הרביעית לפי החלוקה העיקרית של הספירות לחמש (כתר חכמה בינה תפארת ומלכות) והיא מקבילה לבחינה ג' של האור הישר, הוא 'אור חסדים בהארת החכמה', כלומר עיקרו אור החסדים (הנמשך מרצון הנבראים להידבק בבורא) של הבינה, אך מתעורר בו גם רצון מסוים לקבל את אור הבורא, והוא מושך חלק מאור החכמה, האור העליון.

description.en: Mashiach (the Messiah) — literally "anointed one" — generally refers to a savior or liberator figure believed to be a future redeemer of Jews, who ushers in the messianic era. Generations of Jewish texts debate what the messianic era entails, as well as the role that belief in the Messiah should play in Jewish practice. In the Bible, the word *mashiach* is used to refer to kings or high priests, selected by God and anointed with oil.
description.he: משיח - דמות מרכזית בשליחות אלוהים, הנחשבת כגואלת העתידית של עם ישראל, פותחת את העידן המשיחי ומביאה לבסוף לשלום עולמי. מקורות היהדות לאורך הדורות מתווכחים על אופיים של ימות המשיח ועל התפקיד שהאמונה במשיח צריכה למלא. כל המקורות שותפים לציפייה למשיח ולגאולה שמלווה את העם היהודי דורות רבים ומוזכרת פעמים רבות בתפילה ובשאר המקורות. בתנ"ך, המילה *משיח* משמשת להתייחסות למלכים או כוהנים גדולים, שנבחרו על ידי אלוהים ונמשחו בשמן.

description.en: *Avodat Hashem* — ”service of God” in English — is a primary religious objective in many Jewish texts. The first use of the term “service” in relationship to people serving God is in the book of Exodus, describing the expected [worship](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.7.16?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) of the Israelites upon leaving Egypt. In later Jewish sources, *avodat Hashem* takes the form of ritual sacrifices, prayer, general fulfillment of the Torah’s commandments, or ethical character development.
description.he: עבודת השם כוללת סגידה לאל ומילוי החובות הדתיות והרוחניות שבתורה.

description.en: The book of [Exodus](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus?tab=contents) recounts how, after hundreds of years of the Israelites' slavery in Egypt, God miraculously frees the people through a process of [ten plagues](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-ten-plagues?tab=admin) and the splitting of the [Red Sea](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/splitting-of-the-red-sea?tab=admin). The [Passover](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/passover?tab=admin) holiday commemorates these events, and discussing the Exodus is a focal point of the Passover [seder](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/seder?tab=admin).
description.he: יציאת מצרים היא סיפור המתואר בספר שמות בתנ״ך, שבמהלכו יצאו בני ישראל באופן ניסי משעבודו של העם המצרי. הניסים המרכזיים המתוארים בסיפור הם עשרת המכות ששיאם במכת בכורות, וקריעת ים סוף אשר אפשרה לעם ישראל לברוח מהצבא המצרי לכיוון ארץ כנען. חג הפסח מהווה זיכרון ליציאת מצרים, וההגדה של פסח, אשר אותה קוראים בליל הסדר, דנה בהשתלשלות האירועים.

image_caption.he: קריעת ים סוף, פרסקו מבית הכנסת דורא אירופוס, 244-256.

description.en: There were two Jewish Temples, or *battei mikdash* (singular: *beit mikdash*) that stood in ancient Jerusalem. The first was built by [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=admin) and destroyed by the Babylonians in 586 BCE, and the second was built in the late sixth century BCE with the blessing of the Persian Empire and was later destroyed by the Romans in 70 CE. These Temples were the central site of Jewish sacrifice and pilgrimage while they stood. The destruction of these holy Temples was tragic, traumatic, and completely transformational for Jews and Judaism. The Temples and the service of God that took place there are described extensively in Jewish texts, as are their destructions and practices surrounding how they are mourned to this very day.
description.he: בית המקדש נבנה בירושלים בידי שלמה המלך כדי להחליף את המשכן ואת המזבחות האחרים בארץ וכדי לשמש מרכז לחיים היהודיים ולעבודת הפולחן היהודית. החורבן הסופי של המקדש מתואר באריכות במקורות חז"ל.

description.en: Any [level](/topics/level) of reality that incorporates another [level](/topics/level) within it is called the external clothing of the inner [level](/topics/level), and the inner [level](/topics/level) is enclothed within that outer [level](/topics/level). For example, a vessel that contains the light is also the clothing of the light and the light is enclothed within it. Likewise, the body is described as clothing for the soul.

In the Jewish textual tradition, exile (*galut* in Hebrew) is viewed as both a punishment and a way to make amends with God. The tension between exile from and return to Israel is a common theme in Jewish literature — from Abraham's exile to Egypt to the modern return of Jews to the state of Israel.
description.he: עבור העם היהודי הגלות נושאת עימה משמעות כפולה – הן של עונש על חטאים והן של כפרה עליהם. המתח שבין הגלות ובין השיבה אל ארץ ישראל הוא מאפיין שכיח בספרות היהודית, החל בירידתו של אברהם למצרים וכלה בשיבת היהודים אל מדינת ישראל של ימינו.

description.en: The *sefirot* represent ten ways through which the Creator reveals Himself in the creation, with each *sefira* representing a different degree of revelation. The term *sefira* itself has the same root as the word sapir, which means sapphire or radiance, indicating that the divine light is contained within the *sefirot* and illuminates the creation through them.  Generally, there are ten *sefirot*: [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). But in essence there are five primary *sefirot*: [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). Additionally, each of these five *sefirot* are themselves composed of the other *sefirot*, since everything in reality is formed out of *sefirot*. Thus, for example, the *sefira* of [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) contains the [levels](/topics/level) of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1).  As for the five remaining *sefirot*, [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), and [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), they are encompassed within the *sefira* of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). Like the other *sefirot*, the *sefira* of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) contains all five *sefirot*, but in this case they are called by different names: In this context, they are called [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah) and [*Hod*](/topics/hod1). The reason the sefirot are given different names is that a different kind of light from that of the other *sefirot*, called the “light of giving,” is revealed through [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). Although they are named differently, they are still, in a sense, the same five *sefirot* mentioned above. Thus, [*Ḥesed*](/topics/hesed) is referred to as the [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Gevura*](/topics/gevura) as the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah) as the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Hod*](/topics/hod1) as the [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). In addition to these five, there is another *sefira* that incorporates all the [levels](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) called [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1).

description.en: A variation of the term "evil inclination" – *yetzer hara* in Hebrew – is first found in the book of [Genesis](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.6.5?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), as God acknowledges the evil impulse within people. In rabbinic literature, the evil inclination is often discussed in contrast to its opposite, the good inclination (*yetzer hatov* in Hebrew). In some sources, the force is presented as an internal drive within people, while other texts depict the *yetzer hara* as an external figure that can tempt people toward bad choices.

In the Bible, the Hebrew word for "wisdom," *chokhmah,* can take on different meanings depending on context: for example, the word can refer to superior intellect, moral discernment, or excellence with a practical skill. Several biblical characters are described as wise, from [Betzalel](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/betzalel?tab=admin) to the [wise woman from Tekoa](https://www.sefaria.org/II_Samuel.14.2?ven=english|Tanakh:_The_Holy_Scriptures,_published_by_JPS&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) to, perhaps most notably, [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=admin). Later Jewish texts further explore the nature, divine origins, merits, and limitations of wisdom.

description.en: The word Shekhinah, referring to God's imminent presence, comes from the Hebrew root for "dwell." In rabbinic literature, the Shekhinah represents a protective presence that can rest among the people; in Lurianic Kabbalah, “Shekhinah” refers to the feminine aspect of God and carries particular significance in unifying God’s presence in the world. In both rabbinic and kabbalistic literature, the Shekhinah joins the people of Israel in exile, and humans have a role in bringing the presence of God closer or pushing God’s presence further away.
Korach was a Levite who rebelled against Moses's authority. He, his fellow rebels, and their families were all swallowed up by the earth.
description.he: קֹרַח הוא בן שבט לוי שמרד בסמכותו של משה. הוא וְיתר המורדים שהצטרפו אליו קיפחו את חייהם – חלקם נשרפו למוות ואת חלקם בלעה האדמה עם בני משפחותיהם.

description.en: Nebuchadnezzar (prounounced in Hebrew, Nevukhadnetzar) was a Babylonian king who exiled many Judeans, including their then-king Jehoiachin, in 597 BCE and then in 586 BCE conquered Judah and destroyed Jerusalem and [the First Temple](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/destruction-of-the-temple?tab=sources). The book of Daniel describes him as later recognizing God's power and going mad.
description.he: נבוכדנצר הוא ממלכי בבל. הוא כבש את ירושלים והגלה את תושביה לבבל. בספר דניאל מתואר שבתקופה מאוחרת יותר הכיר נבוכדנצר בגדולת אלוהי ישראל ואיבד את שפיותו.

image_caption.he: Nebuchadnezzar before the fiery furnace (Daniel 3:26), Hartwell James 1905, 1916 {PD-US}

description.en: R. Yudan was a teacher and judge who lived in the fourth century in Tiberias, where he studied under Rabbi Abba. Though he appears freqently in the Talmud Yerushalmi and in the Midrash, almost nothing is known about his life or his family. Most of what is recorded from him is in the area of aggadah (non-legal teachings, including biblical interpretation and parables).
description.he: רבי יודן היה דיין ומורה שחי במאה הרביעית בטבריה, שם הוא למד אצל רבי אבא. למרות ששמו מופיע פעמים רבות במדרשים ובירושלמי, כמעט ולא ידוע דבר על קורות חייו ומשפחתו. רוב המידע עליו קשור באגדות (כדוגמת לימוד תורה בניגוד לחוק, פרשנות על התנך ומשלים)

description.en: Daniel is the protagonist of the Book of Daniel. He was taken to the court of Nevukhadnetsar after he conquered Jerusalem. There he rose in the court but prophecied the destruction of Babylonia by Persia. He later had visions regarding the coming Macedonian and Seleucid Greek empires.
description.he: דניאל הוא הגיבור של ספר דניאל המקראי. לאחר כיבוש ירושלים וחורבן העיר על ידי הבבלים הוא נלקח לחצר נבוכדנצר מלך בבל. הוא גדל בבית המלך אך נותר נאמן לאמונתו. הוא ניבא את חורבן בבל על ידי ממלכת פרס ואת עליית האימפריה המקדוני והסלאוקי.

image_caption.he: Daniel at Belshazzar's feast, England [N.W. Midlands]; circa 1375-1400

titles.text: Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi

description.en: Ezekiel was a prophet in the time of the kings Josiah and Jehoiachin who had mystical visions about God's chariot, majesty, and hosts. According to Jewish tradition, accounts of his visions were later written down to make up the book of Ezekiel.
description.he: יחזקאל הוא נביא בתקופת המלכים יאשיהו ויהויכין. נבואותיו מתאפיינות בחזיונות בעלי משמעות מיסטית של מרכבת האל, מלוכתו וצבאותיו. על פי המסורת היהודית, נבואותיו נכתבו כספר בתקופה מאוחרת יותר.

description.en: Eating features from the outset of the Torah in the story of the garden of Eden, where Adam and Eve's [consumption](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.6?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) of forbidden fruit shapes human history. Food serves as a central theme in many other biblical stories: Patriarchs and matriarchs [leave](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.12.10?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&sbsq=%D7%95%D7%99%D7%94%D7%99%20%D7%A8%D7%A2%D7%91%20%D7%91%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%A5&with=SidebarSearch&lang2=en) their homes during [famines](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.26.1?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&sbsq=%D7%95%D7%99%D7%94%D7%99%20%D7%A8%D7%A2%D7%91%20%D7%91%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%A5&with=SidebarSearch&lang2=en) in search of food to eat, Esau sells his birthright to eat a [bowl of soup](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.25.30?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&sbsq=%D7%94%D7%9C%D7%A2%D7%99%D7%98%D7%A0%D7%99&with=SidebarSearch&lang2=en), and the people of Israel repeatedly [complain](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.11.4?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) about food in the desert. Jewish texts explore many commandments and practices surrounding food, including feeding the hungry, reciting blessings before and after eating, observing the laws of kashrut, and eating certain foods during specific occasions (like matzah on Passover, for example).

description.en: Often translated as bounty, flow, or abundance, *shefa* comes from the Hebrew word *hashpa’a*, which in this context means to give. Rays of sunlight, for example, can be described as the sun’s *shefa*. The rays constitute a “flow” of light from the sun that provides light and sustenance to the earth in bountiful abundance. In kabbalistic thought, *shefa* refers to different forms of light that flow from God's essence or from the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) and the like. Additionally, *shefa* can be used to refer both to God’s giving to creation, as well as the giving of created beings to each other.

[The Shema](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Weekday%2C_Shacharit%2C_Blessings_of_the_Shema%2C_Shema?lang=bi), Judaism's most famous prayer, is actually not a prayer at all. Rather it is a declaration of God's unity and other central doctrines of Judaism. It involves reciting three passages from the Torah, one of which is interrupted by another ancient phrase, the origins of which are outside the Bible.
description.he: קריאת שמע היא תפילה ידועה השגורה בפי עם ישראל והיא כוללת שלושה קטעים מפסוקי התורה ומשפט אחד שאינו מן התנ"ך. המילים של קריאת שמע הן הצהרה על ייחוד האל, אהבתו וקבלת עול מצוות. קריאת שמע היא מצווה מהתורה הנאמרת פעמיים ביום, בתפילת שחרית ובתפילת ערבית. רבים שמתו על קידוש השם קראו את קריאת שמע לפני מותם כהצהרה על אמונתם.

description.en: Ahab was the seventh king of the northern Kingdom of Israel, and a wicked one. He allowed foreign worship to flourish under his wife Jezebel's influence, and was willing to arbitrarily dispossess his subjects. He was eventually killed in a military campaign against the Arameans.
description.he: אחאב, המלך השביעי בממלכת ישראל, היה מלך רשע. תחת השפעתה של איזבל אשתו התיר ועודד פריחה של עבודה זרה בתקופתו והסכים לנשל את נתיניו מאדמותיהם באופן שרירותי. נהרג במערכה צבאית נגד הארמים.

image_caption.he: Elijah, Ahab, and Jezebel in Naboth's vineyard, Thomas Rooke, 1880

description.en: Jewish texts approach joy in a number of ways — from the Torah's commanding of Jews to rejoice in certain contexts to joy's characterization as a divine response to humanity's fulfillment of God's will. While joy itself can be a form of serving God, in some instances it can also be a human response to divine action or of being close to God.
description.he: השמחה פרושה לאורך מקורות היהדות כנקודת מוצא חיובית ומומלצת. עם זאת ישנה ביקורת כנגד "שמחת הוללות". לעתים, השמחה עצמה מתוארת כדרך לעבודת השם ולהשגת קרבת אלוהים. בהקשרים מסוימים התורה מצווה לשמוח.

image_caption.he: סוכות, ארתור שיק. 1948

description.en: R. Abba b. Mamal llived in the land of Israel, likely in the lower Galilee. He studied under R. Oshiya and was considered one of the greats of his generation. His discussions with his contemporary, R. Zeira, are found throughout the Yerushalmi.
description.he: רבי אבא בר ממל חי ופעל בארץ ישראל, כנראה בגליל התחתון. הוא למד אצל רבי הושעיה ונחשב לאחד מגדולי הדור. שיחותיו עם רבי זירא החברותא שלו, מופיעים במקומות רבים בתלמוד הירושלמי.

description.en: Isaiah, to whom the book of Isaiah is traditionally attributed, is one of the major biblical prophets. He is known for both prophesying the doom of Israel and its redemption — both politically and in a messianic age.
description.he: ישעיהו הוא אחד הנביאים החשובים במקרא, ומקובל לייחס לו את ספר ישעיהו. הוא נודע בזכות נבואות החורבן והגאולה שלו. נבואותיו משלבות מרכיבים פוליטיים ומשיחיים.

image_caption.en: Isaiah, James Tissot, 1896-1902
image_caption.he: Isaiah, James Tissot, 1896-1902

description.en: Many biblical characters are described as loving their spouses or children. The Torah commands people to love in specific contexts – like loving one’s fellow, the stranger, and God – and [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) consists of poetic conversations between two lovers. Jewish texts composed over thousands of years explore the wonders, hardships, and practical manifestations of love.
description.he: דמויות מקראיות רבות מתוארות כאוהבות את בני זוגן או ילדיהן. התורה מצווה על אנשים לאהוב בהקשרים ספציפיים - כמו אהבת הזולת, הגר והאל וגם פרקי מגילת שיר השירים הם למעשה שיח של שירה בין שני אוהבים. מקורות יהדות שנכתבו לאורך הדורות עוסקים בביטויים המעשיים של אהבה וגם בקשיים שבה.

description.en: R. Hizkiyah learned under R. Yirmiyah and R. Abbahu and was active in Caesarea.
description.he: רבי חזקיה למד אצל רבי ירמיה ורבי אבהו. פעל בקיסריה.

description.en: Elisha was a prophet in the Book of Kings and the successor of Elijah (Eliyahu). He was known as a miracle worker, performing such feats as resurrecting the dead and healing the sick. He also aided and saved the life of the Israelite king Jehoash.
description.he: אלישע היה נביא בספר מלכים ויורשו של אליהו. נודע בתור עושה ניסים, למשל החיה נער מת וריפא חולים. הוא גם סייע ליואש מלך ישראל והציל את חייו.

image_caption.en: Prophet Elisha and the Shunammite woman on Mt. Carmel. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, 1649
image_caption.he: הנביא אלישע והאישה השונמית בהר הכרמל. חרבראנד ואן דן אקהאוט, 1649

description.en: Ishmael was the first son of Abraham, by his concubine Hagar. Acting on Sarah's advice and God's instruction, he and his mother were expelled from their home. An angel reassured them and showed them where to find water and he became the ancestor of the Ishmaelites.
description.he: ישמעאל הוא בנו הבכור של אברהם ובנה של הגר פילגשו. בעקבות עצת שרה וצו האל שולחו ישמעאל והגר מבית אברהם. לאחר שנקלעו למצוקה במדבר, נגלה אליהם מלאך שהוביל אותם לבאר מים ועודד אותם בנוגע לעתידם. ישמעאל הוא אבי העם הישמעאלי.

image_caption.he: Abraham banishes Hagar and Ishmael; Sarah and Isaac look on. Gerard Hoet (1648–1733)

description.en: Rav Giddel was a student of Rav who is often quoted citing his teacher. When the latter died, he first became a student of Rav Huna, but then moved to Israel to study under R. Yochanan.
description.he: רב גידל, תלמידו של רב, פעמים רבות מוזכר מצטט את רבו. אחרי פטירתו של רב היה לתלמידו של רב הונא, אך עלה לארץ ישראל כדי ללמוד אצל רבי יוחנן.

description.en: Shemittah, or the sabbatical year, is the seventh year of the seven-year agricultural cycle mandated by the Torah in the land of Israel. During the Shemittah year, working the land is prohibited, produce that grows on the land takes on sacred status, and debts are forgiven. Shemittah is first mentioned in the Torah in [Exodus 23:10-11](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.23.10?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=he&with=all&lang2=he).

description.en: The [book of Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/Esther) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. It tells the story of [Esther](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/esther), a Jew who becomes queen of Persia and together with her cousin, [Mordekhai](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mordekhai), foils a plot of the evil [Haman](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/haman) to destroy the Jews. To commemorate the transformation from “grief and mourning to festive joy” (9:22), Esther and Mordekhai establish the holiday of [Purim](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/purim). The book of Esther is read publicly in the evening and morning of Purim.
description.he: אחת מחמש המגילות, בה מסופר על השתלשלות האירועים שהובילו לחג הפורים

description.en: Animals are present from the very beginning of the Torah, as they are among God's first creations in the [book of Genesis](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis?tab=contents). Animals feature in a variety of contexts, such as biblical and talmudic stories, legal discussions about how to treat them, and poetic liturgical works that marvel at their wonders.

description.en: Ruth is the protagonist of the [book of Ruth](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-book-of-ruth?tab=sources). Though a Moabite foreigner, she followed her beloved Israelite mother-in-law Naomi to Bethlehem after their husbands died. She committed herself to Naomi and to her God and to the nation of Israel. She marries her late husband's next of kin, and their child was an ancestor of King David.

description.en: In Hebrew, the same word is used to refer both to “song” and “[poem](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/poetry).” The [Hebrew Bible](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Tanakh) includes songs appearing at pivotal moments in the narrative, including the [Song of the Sea](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/song-of-the-sea1) after the crossing of the [Red Sea](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/red-sea), the Song of [Ha’azinu](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/parashat-haazinu) at the end of the journey through the wilderness, and the [Song of Deborah](https://www.sefaria.org/Judges.5) after a victory in the book of Judges. Songs (or poems) also make up books such as the [book of Psalms](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms) and [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs). Jewish [liturgy](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Liturgy) include religious songs composed throughout Jewish history, sometimes called piyyutim. Jewish communities in different times and locations have developed a diversity of traditions of secular and religious singing.

description.en: R. Ya'akov b. Idi lived in Tyre and was considered such a great expert in Jewish law that questions were sent to him even though he lived out of the way. He was a student of R. Yehoshua b. Levi and also of R. Yochanan.
description.he: רבי יעקב בר אידי התגורר בצור ונחשב מומחה גדול בהלכה, עד כדי כך שנשלחו אליו שאלות בהלכה למרות מיקומו המרוחק. היה תלמיד של רבי יהושע בן לוי ושל רבי יוחנן.

description.en: Samson was a judge, Nazirite and military leader in the book of Judges. After victories against the Philistines, he was tricked by his lover, Delilah, into betraying the source of his strength. He was captured and blinded by the Philistines, but he was eventually able to kill many of them, and himself, by destroying their temple.
description.he: שמשון היה שופט, נזיר ומנהיג צבאי בספר שופטים. אחרי שהוביל כמה ניצחונות על הפלישתים, הצליחה דלילה, המאהבת שלו, להערים עליו ולגלות את מקור כוחו. הוא נשבה על ידי הפלישתים שעיוורו את עיניו, אך הצליח להרוג את שוביו ופלישתים רבים אחרים והתאבד כשהחריב את מקדשם.

description.en: Tisha B’Av, the ninth day of the Hebrew month of Av, is a fast day and the saddest day on the Jewish calendar. Among other historical tragedies, it commemorates the destruction of the First and Second Temples in Jerusalem in 586 BCE and 70 CE, respectively. One fasting abstains from food and other physical pleasures, reads the biblical book of Lamentations, and observes mourning customs.
description.he: תשעה באב, החל בט' באב, הוא צום בן 25 שעות שיוצא בדרך כלל ביולי או אוגוסט. יום זה, המצוין על-ידי הימנעות מאכילה, שתייה, רחצה, יחסי מין ומלבושי עור, הוא יום של אבל על חורבן בית המקדש הראשון והשני בירושלים.

description.en: Olam Haba–"the world to come" in English–is a phrase used to describe the afterlife, understood by some as the place where individual souls go upon death and by others as the place where bodies go, together with their souls, in a future time known as [*techiyat hametim*](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/resurrection?tab=admin) (revival of the dead). The world to come is not explicitly mentioned in the Bible, but later sources understand it as a place where divine justice is executed.

description.en: Egypt (Mitzrayim) plays a central role in the Bible, named both as a land of refuge and a land of danger and subjugation, particularly in the Passover narrative. Egypt is complex, both as the birthplace of the Jewish nation and as the one place the Torah tells Jews not to live. Despite this, Jewish communities flourished in Egypt from antiquity until relatively recently.
description.he: למצרים תפקיד חשוב בתנ"ך, והיא מוזכרת בו גם כמקום מפלט וגם כארץ של סכנה ושעבוד, בייחוד בסיפור יציאת מצרים. עבור היהודים מצרים היא תסביך – מצד אחד זהו מקום לידתו של העם היהודי, ומצד שני זהו המקום היחיד שנאסר עליו לגור בו.

description.en: R. Abun b. R. Hiyya was a scholar who lived in the Land of Israel. He studied under R. Yochanan, R. Ilay, and Rabbi Zeira. According to the Talmud, (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:8), he died at the age of 28. His teacher Rabbi Zeira eulogized him with a parable emphasizing that what R. Abun accomplished in 28 years, most students could not accomplish in 100 years.
description.he: רבי אבון בר חייא היה חכם ארץ ישראלי. הוא למד אצל רבי יוחנן, רבי עילאי ורבי זירא. לפי המסופר בתלמוד (ירושלמי ברכות ב,ח) הוא נפטר בגיל 28.הרב שלו, רבי זירא נשא הספד עליו ואמר שהוא הספיק ב28 שנים דברים שאנשים אחרים לא מספיקים במאה שנה.

enBio.value: Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon (Rambam, also know as Maimonides) was perhaps the greatest intellectual and spiritual figure of post-Talmudic Judaism. He wrote indispensable works of philosophy, Halacha, commentary, and responsa. Born in Spain, his family fled while he was still a youth. After an extended period in Morocco, he settled in Egypt, where he became Nagid (leader) of the Jewish community. His works were all foundational in their field. He was the first to produce a comprehensive commentary on the entire Mishnah. His great work of philosophy, Moreh Nevuchim, spawned an entire discipline and had incalculable influence upon enthusiastic promoters and vehement opponents alike. His code of law, Mishneh Torah, is the first and unsurpassed comprehensive code of Jewish law and practice. He also served as court physician to the Muslim leader Saladin. All of his works were written in Judeo-Arabic except for Mishneh Torah, which was written in a magnificent Hebrew. The precision of his expression is legendary. His descendents served as Negidim of Egypt for another four generations.

heBio.value: רבי משה בן מימון (רמב"ם) נחשב לאחד הגדולים בחכמתו וברוחניותו בתקופה הבתר-תלמודית. הוא כתב חיבורים חיוניים במחשבת ישראל, הלכה, פרשנות ושו"תים. נולד בספרד וברח עם משפחתו בעודו ילד. לאחר תקופה ממושכת במרוקו, הוא התיישב במצרים, ושם הפך לנגיד (מנהיג) של הקהילה היהודית. כל יצירתיו מהוות אבני יסוד בתחום שלהן. הרמב"ם היה הראשון שחיבר פרשנות מקיפה למשנה כולה. חיבורו במחשבת ישראל, מורה נבוכים, הביא לעולם דיסציפלינה שלמה והשפיע בצורה בלתי ניתנת לשיעור על תומכים נלהבים ועל מתנגדים חריפים כאחד. חיבורו ההלכתי, המשנה תורה, הוא החיבור ההלכתי מקיף שאין כמותו. הרמב"ם שימש גם כרופא חצר של המנהיג המוסלמי צלאח א-דין. כל יצירותיו נכתבו בערבית-יהודית, חוץ מהמשנה תורה, שנכתבה בעברית משובחת מאוד. הדיוק בצורת הביטוי שלו הוא אגדי. צאצאיו שימשו כנגידים של מצרים לארבעה דורות נוספים.

description.en: Rabbi Moses ben Maimon (Rambam, also known as Maimonides) was perhaps the greatest intellectual and spiritual figure of post-talmudic Judaism. He wrote indispensable works of philosophy, halakhah, commentary, and responsa. Born in Spain, his family fled while he was still a youth. After an extended period in Morocco, he settled in Egypt, where he became the *naggid* (leader) of the Jewish community. His works were all foundational in their field. He was the first to produce a comprehensive commentary on the entire Mishnah. His great work of philosophy, *Moreh Nevukhim,* spawned an entire discipline and had incalculable influence upon enthusiastic promoters and vehement opponents alike. His code of law, *Mishneh Torah,* is the first and unsurpassed comprehensive code of Jewish law and practice. He also served as court physician to the Muslim leader Saladin. All of his works were written in Judeo-Arabic except for Mishneh Torah, which was written in a magnificent Hebrew. The precision of his expression is legendary. His descendants served as the leaders of the Egyptian Jewish community for another four generations.

description.en: Neshama

Ovyut denotes thickness, materiality, or darkness, as opposed to purity, clarity, and spirituality. In kabbalistic terminology, it expresses the quality of the vessel, which is the will to receive. It is considered thick and dark because it is the antithesis of the eternal divine light, the essence of which is entirely giving. A greater will to receive is regarded as having greater opacity, while a vessel that contains a lesser will to receive is regarded as being more pure. This is because the greater the will to receive that a vessel acquires, the more it is distanced from the Creator and His light and the more material and dark it becomes.

The haggadah is the classic ritual text that serves as the base and script of the Passover seder. Its text was compiled during the periods of the Mishnah and the Talmud, with later medieval additions. It is the most printed Jewish book as new editions and new commentaries are published every year. Different communities around the world have also developed their own variations and ritual practices, often recorded in the editions produced in their own communities.
description.he: ההגדה היא טקסט יהודי קלאסי המהווה את הבסיס לליל הסדר. רובה של ההגדה נכתבה במהלך תקופת המשנה והתלמוד. כיום, ההגדה קיימת בנוסחים רבים בקהילות שונות אשר הוסיפו להגדה פיוטים ותפילות שונות במרוצת הדורות. ההגדה מחולקת ל-14 חלקים אשר המרכזים בהם הינם: קדש - קידוש היום, מגיד - רוב המלל שבהגדה המתאר את סיפור יציאת מצרים, מוציא מצה והלל.

description.en: Jerusalem — Yerushalayim in Hebrew — is considered the holiest city in the Jewish textual tradition. Although it is not mentioned explicitly in the Torah, the book of Deuteronomy refers numerous times to "the place that God will choose," a phrase later sources understood to refer to Jerusalem. In the book of Samuel, [King David](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-david?tab=sources) captured Jerusalem from the Jebusites, and the book of Kings recounts that [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources) built the Temple there. Jerusalem is a central focus of many Jewish prayers, customs, and texts.
description.he: ירושלים הייתה עיר יבוסית שכבש דוד המלך והפך לעיר הבירה של ממלכת ישראל המאוחדת. כאשר בנה שלמה המלך את בית המקדש בירושלים, הייתה העיר לסמל בלתי מעורער של העם היהודי ושל הקשר שלו לאלוהיו.

description.en: The [Mishnah](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Mishnah) is the first major work of rabbinic literature, consisting of teachings transmitted over hundreds of years and compiled around 200 CE. It covers agricultural, ritual, civil, criminal, and Temple-related laws, presenting a multiplicity of legal opinions and incorporating occasional stories. It is a foundation of the Jewish oral tradition, which continues with the [Talmud](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Talmud/Bavli), a work that is structured as commentary on the Mishnah.

description.en: Yom Tov (literally: "good day") refers to any Jewish holiday marked by ritual blessings over the wine and abstention from work: the beginning and end of Passover, Shavuot, Rosh HaShanah, Yom Kippur, the beginning and end of Sukkot, Shemini Atseret, and Simchat Torah.
description.he: יום טוב הוא כל חג יהודי שבו מקדשים על היין ונמנעים ממלאכה: היום הראשון והאחרון של פסח, שבועות, ראש השנה, יום כיפור, היום הראשון והאחרון של סוכות, שמיני עצרת (בחו"ל) ושמחת תורה

description.en: There are assorted fast days scattered across the Jewish calendar. During the two major fast days, Yom Kippur and Tisha B'Av, one abstains from food, drink, washing, and sexual relations for 25 hours. During the other, minor fast days, one abstains from food and drink from sunup to sundown.
description.he: ישנם ימי צום קבועים המפוזרים לאורך לוח השנה היהודי. בשני הצומות המרכזיים, יום כיפור ותשעה באב, נמנעים מאכילה, שתייה, רחצה, יחסי אישות ונעילת נעלי עור למשך 25 שעות. בצומות הקלים יותר נמנעים מאכילה ושתייה מעלות השחר ועד צאת הכוכבים.

description.en: Rachel is one of the four matriarchs of the Jewish people. The beloved and favored wife of [Jacob](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jacob?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), who was tricked into first marrying her older sister [Leah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/leah?tab=sources), Rachel suffered from infertility before giving birth to Jacob's two favored sons, Joseph and Benjamin. She died giving birth to Benjamin.
description.he: רחל היא אחת מארבע האימהות של עם ישראל. היא אשתו האהובה והבכירה של יעקב, שנישא קודם לכן לאחותה לאה. רחל סבלה מעקרות ממושכת לפני שילדה את שני בניו הצעירים והאהובים ביותר של יעקב, יוסף ובנימין. היא מתה בשעת לידתו של בנימין.

description.en: *Keter* is the name of the first and highest [sefira](/topics/sefira2) of the ten [sefirot](/topics/sefirot). However, *Keter* is not always counted as one of the ten [sefirot](/topics/sefirot). Just as a crown, a *keter*, on a person’s head encompasses him but is not part of his body, so too the [sefira](/topics/sefira2) of *Keter*, due to its lofty status, can be considered above the ten [sefirot](/topics/sefirot). When *Keter* is regarded as part of the system, it is the highest part of the [head](/topics/head2), which is comprised of the first three [levels](/topics/level): *Keter*, [Ḥokhma](/topics/hokhma1), and [*Bina*](/topics/bina3). When *Keter* is not included in the list of [sefirot](/topics/sefirot), it is substituted by *Da’at*, a structure that can be considered a pseudo-*sefira*.

Miracles feature throughout the Jewish textual tradition. Supernatural events appear throughout the Bible, including the [ten plagues](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-ten-plagues?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), the [splitting of the sea](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/splitting-of-the-red-sea?tab=sources), and when the walls of [Jericho](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/jericho?tab=sources) fell, among others. Miracles feature in later rabbinic texts as well, and ancient through contemporary works analyze the nature and significance of miracles.
description.he: ניסים מופיעים לאורך כל מסורת ההספרות היהודית. אירועים על-טבעיים מופיעים לאורך התנ"ך, כמו עשר המכות, קריעת ים סוף ונפילת חומות יריחו . ניסים מופיעים גם במקורות יהדות מימי המשנה והתלמוד, ואף בחיבורים מאוחרים יותר.מקורות רבים עוסקים בתפקידו של הנס ומשמעותו.

description.en: The Hebrew word for "peace," *shalom,* is related to the Hebrew word that means whole or perfect, *shalem.* This suggests that there is a relationship between peace and wholeness. Judaism values peace very highly, prioritizing it over nearly everything else, as is reflected in biblical, rabbinic, liturgical, ethical, and legal texts.
description.he: שלום הוא ערך מרכזי בתפיסת העולם היהודית ומופיע במגוון הקשרים במקורות היהדות. ברכת השלום חותמת את תפילת העמידה, את תפילת הקדיש והמילה "שלום" היא אחת משמותיו של האל. בספרי היהדות לאורך הדורות השלום נתפס כמצב אידיאלי והרמוני כאשר המחלוקת לגביו היא כיצד ניתן להשיגו, עד כמה נכון לוותר ולהתפשר עבורו וכיצד להכריע כאשר יש קונפליקט בין האמת והשלום.

description.en: Mar Ukva was among the first of the exilarchs - administrative leaders of the Jewish community in Babylonia who claimed descent from the House of David. He was an important judge and scholar and a student of Shmuel. Known for his piety and wealth, he was famous for his discretion and generosity.
description.he: מר עוקבא היה מראשוני "ראשי הגולה"– המנהיגים האדמיניסטרטיביים של הקהילה היהודית בבבל שטענו שהם צאצאי בית דוד. הוא היה שופט חשוב, חכם גדול ותלמיד של שמואל. נודע בחסידותו ובעושרו וכן בהקפדתו לתת צדקה בסתר.

description.en: Tzara'at is a biblical disease that involved discoloration of one's skin, home, or clothing. Once confirmed by a priest's inspection, it renders the subject ritually impure, requiring them to leave the camp for a period, undergo further inspection, and then a purification process. Tzara'at is the subject of [Leviticus 13–14](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.13?lang=bi&aliyot=0). Several biblical stories have characters inflicted with tzara'at. And tzara'at is the subject of the Mishnah's tractate [Negaim](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Negaim?tab=contents).

description.en: Shortly after the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai, despairing that their leader Moses had died atop the mountain, the Israelites built and began to worship a golden calf — in direct violation of the first commandments of the [Ten Commandments](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.20.3?lang=bi&aliyot=0). The "golden calf" may refer to either the idol the Israelites built or [the narrative](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.32?lang=bi&aliyot=0). Upon Moses' discovery of the Israelites' grievous transgression, he smashed the tablets of the law, ground up the golden calf, and made the Israelites drink the mixture.

description.en: Blessings are declarations of acknowledgement to God about His greatness, His gifts or His connection with the Jewish people via the commandments. While they follow several formats, they all include the key phrase, "Blessed are You, O Lord!"

description.en: R. Yehudah b. Pazi was the son and student of R. Shimon b. Pazi. As he grew into an outstanding scholar and judge, other scholars would inquire about his father's teachings from him.

description.en: Wine (yayin, in Hebrew) is widely discussed in biblical and rabbinic sources, with the focus being on its enjoyment as well as its potential for abuse. On Shabbat, as well as on Jewish holidays, special prayers are said over wine in order to fulfill the biblical commandment of sanctifying the day.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Yesod* is the ninth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Yesod* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1).  *Yesod* is the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) that represents the end of the middle line or column, the line of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). Accordingly, *Yesod* is a unique aspect of the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) and also exists in parallel in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1), which receives the lights of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1). *Yesod*, which means “Foundation,” is named thus because it includes the “foundations” of its [level](/topics/level), meaning the various lights within that [level](/topics/level). It then transmits these lights to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) below it, so that *Yesod* serve as the foundation for the existence of the feminine aspect of the [level](/topics/level). In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which correlate to the human body, the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Yesod* represents the sexual reproductive organs.

Kashrut means “fitness” and refers to the dietary laws governing what is permitted and forbidden for consumption. These laws further prescribe how kosher food should be prepared and by whom. While the Torah dictates which animals may be consumed and under what conditions, the rabbis further derived principles to ensure that one does not violate the Torah and discuss the value of these practices.

description.en: The Torah commands [“Justice, justice you shall pursue”](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.16.20?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) as a condition for inhabiting the land of Israel. The Torah further commands specific measures to be put in place in order to establish just societies, including just courts and fair and honest weights and measures. Several biblical prophets critique those who prioritize ritual practice but ignore the Torah’s imperatives to act justly, and sources throughout the rabbinic tradition discuss and analyze the requirements and parameters of justice.

description.en: Treating others with kindness is a foundational Jewish practice and is considered one of [three pillars on which the world stands](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.1.2?lang=bi). Biblical characters like Abraham exemplify kindness in their generous treatment of strangers, and [rabbinic texts](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.14a.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) instruct people to follow God’s example of behaving with kindness.

description.en: Tefillin are black leather boxes that contain small parchment scrolls on which specific passages from the Torah are written. Tefillin are worn on the upper arm and forehead, usually during morning prayers, except on Shabbat and holidays, as the means of fulfilling the commandment to "bind them as a sign on your hand and as a symbol between your eyes" [(Deuteronomy 6:8)](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.6.8?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).
description.he: תפילין הן קופסות עור שחורות ובתוכן מגילות קלף של פסוקים מן התורה. יהודים מגיל בר מצווה מניחים את התפילין על הזרוע ועל המצח מדי יום חול לפחות פעם אחת ביום החל בתפילת שחרית.

description.en: Rav Hama b. Hanina was a teacher in the time of R. Yochanan and possibly the son of R. Hanina b. Hama. Not much is known about him, but we are told that he used his wealth to build a synagogue in Sepphoris.

description.en: Evil speech — *lashon hara,* in Hebrew — refers to the prohibition against speech that is harmful to another person, even though it may be true. The parameters, laws, and spiritual implications of *lashon hara* are discussed throughout the Jewish textual tradition and are a focus of Rabbi Yisrael Meir Kagan's [Chafetz Chaim](https://www.sefaria.org/Chafetz_Chaim?tab=contents), the first work to organize the laws of proper speech comprehensively.

Traditional Jewish sources [describe](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.14a.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) how 48 prophets and seven prophetesses prophesied on behalf of the people of Israel. Many of their teachings are recorded in the Prophets section of the Bible, which consists of collections of prophetic speeches and narrative accounts of history attributed to prophets. These prophets covered the period from the people of Israel's entrance into the land of Israel through the beginning of the Second Temple. In the Torah, [Abraham](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.20.8?lang=bi&aliyot=0) and [Moses](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.34.10?lang=bi&aliyot=0) are also called prophets, and the Torah warns against listening to a [false prophet](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.13.2?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).

The light of giving (*or ḥassadim*) is the type of [*shefa*](/topics/shefa1)  that is revealed as a result of the will or desire of a created being to give. This light originates in the second [level](/topics/level) of the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot), the [level](/topics/level) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3). This is in contrast to the other type of [*shefa*](/topics/shefa1), the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), which is the light of the Creator that emanates in and from the first [level](/topics/level) of the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot), the [level](/topics/level) of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). Although the light of giving is not the main lifeforce of the created beings, it contains an important quality related to the [constriction](/topics/constriction) (*tzimtzum*). Constriction involves the abstention of the vessel of the will to receive (the vessel of [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1)) from receiving the light of the Creator. However, this [constriction](/topics/constriction) of the vessel applies only to the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). The receiving vessel for the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) is the will of the created being to receive. After the [constriction](/topics/constriction) this vessel is disqualified as a vessel for the divine light. However, [constriction](/topics/constriction) does not apply to the light of giving, whose vessel is the will of the created being to give. One result of this difference in the effects of the [constriction](/topics/constriction) is that the light of giving illuminates in places and ways where the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) does not shine. Additionally, by [enclothing](/topics/enclothe) the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) in the light of giving, the light of giving helps the light of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) illuminate [levels](/topics/level) from which it would otherwise be restricted.

The head refers to the highest part of a [level](/topics/level). For example, in each [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1), the first three [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are considered the head of that [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1). Additionally, the root of every [level](/topics/level) may also be defined as its head. This might occur when the [returning light](/topics/returning-light1) resulting from a [*fusion through collision*](/topics/fusion-through-collision) with a [partition](/topics/partition2) [enclothed](/topics/enclothe) the supernal light. While this process ultimately allows for the [returning light](/topics/returning-light1) to serve as a complete vessel for the supernal light, initially it only serves as the conceptual root of that actualized vessel. This initial stage of [enclothing](/topics/enclothe) of the supernal light by the [returning light](/topics/returning-light1) is called the head of the particular [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1).

Amalek was the first nation to attack the Israelites in the desert, attacking them from behind so as to target the weak and weary stragglers. As a result of this, paradoxically, the Torah commands the Israelites simultaneously to remember what they did and to blot out even the memory of them.
description.he: עמלק הוא עם שהתקיף את בני ישראל במדבר. העמלקי התקיף מאחור ושם לו למטרה את החלשים בעם. בשל מעשה זה התורה מצווה על בני ישראל לזכור לנצח את עמלק ובד בבד למחות את שמו.
