description.en: In the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible), work can be seen as part of the human experience from the outset: When God creates man, God puts him in the garden of Eden to ["work it and preserve it."](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.2.15?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en) When Adam and Eve later sin by eating from the tree of knowledge, Adam is cursed with a future of arduous labor: ["By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread"](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.19?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en). In describing the commandment of Shabbat, the Torah contrasts Shabbat with weekdays, which are described as [days of work](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.35.2?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en_). Rabbinic and later texts delve into the question of whether work is intrinsically valuable, how to balance work and other values, and the proper ways to treat workers.

image_caption.en: An Israeli stamp quoting Pirkei Avot 2:2, saying that studying the Torah without combined labor leads to idleness. Israel, 1972
image_caption.he: An Israeli stamp quoting Pirkei Avot 2:2, saying that studying the Torah without combined labor leads to idleness. Israel, 1972

description.en: Ki Teitzei (“When You Go Out”) contains numerous laws, more than appear in any other Torah portion. These include laws about the treatment of a captive woman, returning lost objects, forbidden mixtures, the erection of a rooftop fence, rape, collateral, and workers’ wages.
description.he: בפרשת כי תצא מספר הדינים הגדול ביותר בהשוואה לכל פרשה אחרת בתורה. במצוות מפורטים דיני ירושה ודיני קבורת המת, מצוות השבת אבדה ודינים אחרים להתנהלות חברתית מוסרית, כמו מתנות עניים, איסור ריבית ואיסור הלנת שכר. מתוארים גם דיני משפחה כמו דיני נישואין, גירושין, אישות, ייבום וחליצה.

description.en: The prophet Zechariah, active during the post-exilic period, emphasized themes of repentance, divine mercy, and visions symbolizing the restoration and future glory of Jerusalem and the Jewish people.
description.he: זכריה היה נביא בתקופת דריווש מלך פרס. נבואותיו נגעו לימות המשיח.

description.en: Beshalach (“When He Let Go”) describes the splitting of the Red Sea and the song the Israelites sing upon crossing through. In the desert, God sweetens bitter water and provides manna and quail. The portion ends recounting the victory of the Israelites against an attack by the Amalekites.
description.he: בפרשת בשלח מתוארות קריעת ים סוף, טביעת חיל מצרים, הצלת בני ישראל ושירת הים ששרו משה ובני ישראל על ים סוף, וכן שירת מרים. בני ישראל מגיעים למדבר ומתלוננים, ואלוהים ממתיק להם מים מרים ומספק להם מן ושליו לאכול. משה מכה בצור ברפידים ומוציא ממנו מים, ויהושע מנהיג שם את העם במלחמה נגד עמלק.

image_caption.he: טביעת פרעה בים סוף, לוקאס קראנאך האב, 1530 גרמניה, WikiArt

description.en: Parashat Korach recounts the rebellion of Korach (a cousin of Moses and Aaron), Dathan, Abiram, and 250 of their followers. Some rebels are swallowed by the ground, while others are consumed by a fire from God and others die in a plague. The portion ends by describing gifts given to priests and Levites.
description.he: בפרשת קרח מתואר כיצד קרח, דתן ואבירם ו-250 מנהיגים נוספים מערערים על מנהיגות משה ועל כהונת אהרן ומובילים נגדם מרד. אלוהים מעניש את המורדים: חלקם נשרפים באש וחלקם נבלעים באדמה בדרך נס. העימות מסתיים בפריחת מטה אהרן, המוכיחה את בחירתו על ידי האל, ובסוף הפרשה מובא ציווי על מתנות כהונה ולווייה.

description.en: The Garden of Eden features in the opening chapters of the book of [Genesis](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis?tab=contents). God plants the garden, causes trees to grow there, and places Adam in the garden to work and preserve it. After [Eve and Adam](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam-and-eve?tab=sources) eat forbidden fruit, God drives them out. The Garden of Eden has been the subject of analysis and discussion throughout thousands of years of the Jewish textual tradition.

description.en: Biblical and rabbinic texts often talk of living into old age as a [blessing](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.15.15?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he), a [reward](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.6.2?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) for fulfilling the commandments, and a stage of life marked by wisdom. The Torah instructs people to show [deference to the old](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.19.32?lang=he&aliyot=0), a commandment many see as a central Jewish value. Some texts also discuss [difficult](https://www.sefaria.org.il/Shabbat.151b.11?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) experiences that can accompany old age, like a [sense of futility](https://www.sefaria.org/II_Samuel.19.36?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he), frustration at not being able to enjoy life’s pleasures, and [fears](https://www.sefaria.org.il/Psalms.71.9?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=he) surrounding death and loneliness.

description.en: Tazria (“She Bears Seed”) opens by describing the purification process for a woman after childbirth. It then describes different forms of *tzara’at*, a discoloration condition on skin or clothing, and the requirement of an infected person to dwell alone outside the camp and be inspected by a priest.
description.he: בפרשת תזריע מפורטים דיני היולדת – טומאתה, טהרתה והקורבנות שהיא מביאה למשכן. רוב הפרשה עוסקת בטומאת צרעת: זיהוי סוגי צרעת בגוף האדם ודיני המצורע הטמא. את הצרעת מאבחן כהן, שנדרש לראות את הנגע ולקבוע את דינו. הפרשה מסתיימת בזיהוי סוגי טומאת צרעת הבגד ודיניה.

description.en: Yitro (“Jethro”) begins as Moses reunites with his father-in-law Yitro and accepts his advice to appoint judges who will help govern the Israelites. The Israelites prepare to encounter God at Mount Sinai. God descends amidst fire, smoke, thunder, and the blast of a shofar and gives the Ten Commandments.
description.he: יתרו חותן משה מופיע במחנה ישראל עם ציפורה בתו ושני בניה לאחר ששמע על הניסים שחולל אלוהים לישראל ביציאת מצרים. יתרו נחשף להנהגתו של משה ומציע לו להקים מערכת משפט יעילה יותר. משה מכין את העם לקבלת התורה בהר סיני ומרחיק את בני ישראל מההר. אלוהים מתגלה לעיני העם בעשן ואש על ראש ההר במעמד עוצמתי המלווה בקולות וברקים וקול שופר ונותן לעם את עשרת הדיברות.

description.en: Rav Hanan b. Rava was the son-in-law of Rav and the father-in-law of Rav Chisda.

description.en:
It is known that as a result of the expansion of the [points](/topics/points) of [*Sag*](/topics/sag) to [*Mah*](/topics/mah1) and [*Ban*](/topics/ban) of the inner [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2), [traces](/topics/traces) of two levels are joined in the [partition](/topics/partition2). These are the first *heh* in [*Sag*](/topics/sag), and the bottom *heh* in the inner [*Adam Kadmon*](/topics/adam-kadmon2). Thus, the [partition](/topics/partition2) is incorporated from two females, [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1). For this reason the [partition](/topics/partition2) was given the name feminine waters, since from this point onwards it incorporates these two females in every [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision) it performs with the supernal light (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 6, Q & A 15). 
The meaning of feminine waters is that it causes a [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision). It is always an expression of [*Netzaḥ*](/topics/netzah), [*Hod*](/topics/hod1), and [*Yesod*](/topics/yesod1), or *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba). For the female is instituted in the [light](/topics/light2) of the [back side](/topics/back-side) of *Imma*, which is attached only to the [light of giving](/topics/light-of-giving) and which rebuffs [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). Accordingly, she does not turn her face towards the male to receive the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), unless she is forced by some factor to do so. This factor is an expression of *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba), to which the [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) has a connection, to illuminate it with the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), due to the relationship between [*Bina*](/topics/bina3) and the *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba) of the [direct light](/topics/direct-light1). Consequently, when the *Ze’ir* and [*Nukba*](/topics/nukba) ascends to her for feminine waters, her [back side](/topics/back-side) immediately stops, and she turns her face to the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), to receive from it the illumination of [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1). She thus engages in a face-to-face [fusion](/topics/fusion-through-collision) with it (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 7, Q & A 35).

The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Ḥesed* is the fourth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Ḥesed* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Keter*](/topics/keter1) [level](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)). The term *sefirat* *Ḥesed* is also a reference to different [levels](/topics/level) and *sefirot* in lower structures of reality that are all derivatives of the root *sefira* of *Ḥesed* found in the [*direct light*](/topics/direct-light1). This [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) is called *Ḥesed* because it contains the light of giving (*ḥassadim*) that emanates from the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), which precedes *Ḥesed*, the light that is the essence of giving and bestowal on the part of a created being and that did not undergo any constriction. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Ḥesed* is always presented as the right hand of the *partzuf*, the hand that represents bestowal and closeness.

Curses are discussed in a variety of contexts throughout the Jewish textual tradition: biblical passages describe [attempts](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.23.7?lang=en&with=all&lang2=en) of [individuals](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.24.11?ven=The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=en&with=all&lang2=en) to curse others, [God's curses](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.26.14?lang=en&with=all&lang2=en) for those who don't follow the commandments, and [several](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.19.14?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=en&with=all&lang2=en) [injunctions](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.22.27?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=en&with=all&lang2=en) against cursing specific [people](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.21.17?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=en&with=Navigation&lang2=en). Rabbinic texts detail and analyze the legal prohibitions of cursing and its implications, and texts of Jewish thought discuss the spiritual ramifications of cursing.

Pinchas opens with God’s promise of a “covenant of peace” for the zealot Pinchas, followed by a census. The daughters of Tzelofchad request and receive new laws regarding inheritance. God instructs Moses to prepare Joshua for leadership, and God describes sacrifices brought daily and on special occasions.
description.he: פרשת פינחס פותחת בהבטחת האל להביא ברית שלום לפינחס לאחר מעשה הקנאות שלו. משה ואלעזר עורכים מפקד חדש. בנות צלפחד מבקשות לקבל את נחלת אביהן בארץ, מאחר שלא היו לו בנים. לקראת מותו משה דואג לעתידו של העם, ואלוהים ממנה את יהושע בן נון למנהיג תחת משה. בסוף הפרשה מפורטים קורבן התמיד וקורבנות המוספים של שבת, ראש חודש ומועדי השנה.

description.en: Vayechi (“He Lived”) is the final Torah portion in the Book of Genesis. It opens as Jacob prepares for his death, making his son Joseph swear to bury him in the Cave of Machpelah. Jacob blesses Joseph’s two sons and his own 12 sons and then dies. Jacob’s sons bury him. The portion ends with Joseph’s death.
description.he: פרשת ויחי היא הפרשה האחרונה בספר בראשית. יעקב מתכונן למותו ומשביע את יוסף שיקבור אותו עם אבותיו במערת המכפלה. יעקב מברך את שני בני יוסף ואת 12 בניו, ומת. בני יעקב קוברים אותו בארץ כנען. אחי יוסף חוששים שאחרי מות יעקב יתנקם בהם יוסף על כל מה שעשו לו. יוסף סולח לאחיו ומשביע אותם שיקברו אותו בארץ כנען. הפרשה מסתיימת בתיאור מותו של יוסף.

description.en: R. Assi is one of the names mentioned most frequently in the Babylonian and Jerusalem Talmud. R. Assi studied under Shmuel in Babylonia before coming to study together with R. Ami in the academy of R. Yochanan in Tiberias. The Babylonian Talmud reports that when he died, all trees were uprootsd (Moed Katan 25b), while the Jerusalem Talmud records that on that day a fountain of Tiberias fell (Avodah Zarah 3:1).
description.he: רבי אסי הוא אחד ששמם מופיע מספר הפעמים הרב ביותר בתלמוד הירושלמי והבבלי. רבי אסי למד אצל שמואל בבבל ולאחר מכן עבר לטבריה כדי ללמוד בבית מדרשו של רבי יוחנן בטבריה יחד עם רבי אמי. בתלמוד הבבלי מסופר שכאשר הוא נפטר שורשי העצים ניתקו ממקומם (מועד קטן כ״ה עמוד ב׳), ובירושלמי מסופר שבאותו יום נעתקה ממקומה מזרקה בטבריה (מסכת עבודה זרה ג׳, א׳)

description.en: Clothing features from the opening chapters of the Torah: Adam and Eve are created without clothing and don't feel embarrassed, but after they eat from the tree of knowledge, they make clothing for themselves out of [fig leaves](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.7?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Clothing features in other biblical narratives and laws: Jacob makes a special coat for his favored son, Joseph; the book of Exodus describes the unique clothing to be worn by priests and the high priest in the Tabernacle; and various biblical figures tear their clothes in mourning, among other instances. Later Jewish sources discuss the significance of clothing and analyze how clothing intersects with themes of holiness, protection, purity, and identity.

description.en: Shem was one of the sons of Noah who was saved during the flood and became the ancestor of several nations, including the Hebrews.

description.en: Taharah is ritual purity and contrasts to tumah, ritual impurity. While the Temples stood, one needed to be in a state of ritual purity to enter the Temple and offer a sacrifice. To attain such a status, depending on the nature of the impurity contracted, the purification process may have entailed a waiting period, sprinkling with the ashes of a [red heifer](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/parah-adumah?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), and immersion in a [mikveh](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mikveh?sort=Relevance&tab=sources). Purity and impurity are the focus of [Seder Toharot](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Mishnah). While most of these laws are no longer observed in the absence of the Temple, some still are.

Chukat (“Law Of”) opens by describing the process of burning the red heifer and using its ashes for purification. It also tells the stories of the deaths of Miriam and Aaron, Moses’ striking of a rock to bring forth water, a plague of venomous snakes, and battles against the Emorite kings Sihon and Og.
description.he: בפרשת חקת מפורט תהליך טהרת האדם מטומאת מת באפר פרה אדומה. מרים מתה, והעם מתלונן שהוא צמא למים. אלוהים מצווה את משה לדבר אל הסלע, ומשה מכה בסלע להוציא ממנו מים. משה ואהרן נענשים שלא יזכו להיכנס לארץ, ואהרן מת בהר ההר. העם מתלונן על האוכל במדבר ונענש במתקפת נחשים. העם מנצח במלחמה נגד סיחון ועוג שני מלכי האמורי בעבר הירדן המזרחי.

description.en: Rabbinic texts describe how the first humans discovered fire, and fire plays a role in many biblical stories, like that of the [burning bush](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/burning-bush?tab=sources). Fire features both physically and metaphorically in Jewish sources; fire serves, for example, as a metaphor for Torah in some rabbinic texts.

description.en: Vayeitzei (“He Went Out”) opens as Jacob dreams about angels going up and down a ladder, and then continues on his journey toward the home of his uncle Laban. During years of indentured servitude, Jacob marries Laban’s daughters Leah and Rachel, bearing children with them and with their maidservants, Bilhah and Zilpah.
description.he: בפרשת ויצא מתואר חלום יעקב, ובו מלאכים עולים בסולם ויורדים בו. יעקב ממשיך בדרכו לבית לבן אחי אימו, ושם הוא מכיר את בת דודו רחל ומבקש להתחתן איתה. לבן מסכים בתנאי שיעקב יעבוד אצלו. אחרי שבע שנים לבן מרמה את יעקב ונותן לו את בתו הבכירה לאה במקום את רחל, אך לאחר משא ומתן מסכים לתת לו לאישה גם את רחל. לאה ורחל ושפחותיהן בלהה וזלפה יולדות ליעקב ילדים.

description.en: The world of *Yetzira* is the third of the four worlds (after the supernal world of *Adam Kadmon*) that emanate and descend from one another in the process of creation. Some maintain that its name derives from the Hebrew words for form, *tzura*, or image, *tziyur*, since it is a kind of image or pattern for the final and fourth world, [*Asiya*](/topics/asiya2). Each of the worlds corresponds to one of the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). The world of *Yetzira* corresponds to the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) or the third [level](/topics/level) of creation. The created beings that dwell in this [level](/topics/level) are the angels called *ḥayot*.
God's direction of the universe.

Mishpatim (“Laws”) recounts a series of God’s laws that Moses gives to the Israelites. These include laws about treatment of slaves, damages, loans, returning lost property, the Sabbath, the sabbatical year, holidays, and destroying idolatry. The portion ends as Moses ascends Mount Sinai for 40 days.
description.he: פרשת משפטים כוללת מספר גדול של דינים ומצוות שאלוהים מצווה את בני ישראל באמצעות משה. הדינים עוסקים בתחומים רבים, כגון עבדות, נזיקין, השבת אבדה, שבת, שמיטה, חגים, איסור עבודה זרה ועוד. בסוף הפרשה מתוארים מעמד כריתת הברית בין אלוהים לעם ועליית משה להר סיני ל40 יום ו40 לילה.

description.en: Birds feature in the Jewish textual tradition from the opening chapter of the Torah, which [recounts](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.1.21?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) how birds were created on the fifth day of creation. [Noah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/noah?tab=admin) uses birds to help determine whether it is safe to leave the ark, and other parts of the Torah discuss laws surrounding birds, like which ones are prohibited for consumption and the obligation to send away a mother bird before taking her young. Later Jewish texts expand on these concepts and other aspects of the nature and qualities of birds.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Gevura* is the fifth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Gevura* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1) [level](/topics/level) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1))  The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Gevura* is called by this name since it characterizes restraint and constriction. It represents the left column in a process called the rectification of lines, and it is this left column on which the [constriction](/topics/constriction) ([*tzimtzum*](/topics/tzimtzum1)) acts. This placement characterizes the power of restraint that is used to repel the supernal light. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Gevura* is generally presented as the left hand of the *partzuf*.

Covenants are binding commitments made between two parties. The most famous covenants in Tanakh are those that God made with Abraham, these include the ["covenant between the parts"](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.15.2?lang=bi&aliyot=0)  and that of [circumcision](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/circumcision?tab=sources). People too can make covenants, as was the case when Abraham made [one with Abimelekh](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.21.23?lang=bi&aliyot=0).
description.he: בריתות הן התחייבויות שנעשו בין שני צדדים. הבריתות המפורסמות ביותר בתנ"ך הן אלו שכרת ה' עם אברהם, הכוללות את "ברית בין הבתרים" וזו של ברית המילה. גם אנשים יכולים לכרות בריתות, כפי שקרה כאשר אברהם כרת ברית עם אבימלך.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Netzaḥ* is the seventh of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – *Keter*, *Ḥokhma*, *Bina*, *Tiferet*, and *Malkhut* – *Netzaḥ* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level) for the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)).  *Netzaḥ* is the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) that completes a structure called the right-hand column in every [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) or world. It is the fourth (thus, the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level)) [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) [level](/topics/level) within the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) (see [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1)). Its essence is therefore that of the [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) [level](/topics/level) which is revealed in the lower part of every *sefira*. As a result, it is considered a “male” [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2), that is, a giving and bestowing [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2), like *Tiferet*. The name *Netzaḥ* comes from the word for victory, *nitzaḥon*. *Netzaḥ* conquers impurity, meaning that, although it is in contact with lower aspects of existence, it simultaneously has the quality of bestowal and giving. This illustrates that *Netzaḥ* is not only undamaged by its involvement in lower realities, but it actually thrives and dominates. In the structure of [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which is analogous to the human body, *Netzaḥ* is generally presented as the right leg of the [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1).

description.en: The High Priest was the head priest of the Israelites, beginning with the biblical [Aaron](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/aaron?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) and continuing through the Second Temple period. The High Priest had a special role in the [Mishkan](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources) and Temple service, and wore unique garments detailed in the [book of Exodus](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.28.3?ven=The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).

description.en: Vayishlach (“He Sent”) follows Jacob and his family as Jacob wrestles with a man (commonly understood as an angel), is renamed Israel, and reconciles with his brother, Esau. Jacob’s daughter, Dina, is raped by a Hivite prince, and her brothers sack a city in response. Rachel dies as she gives birth to Jacob's youngest child, Benjamin.
description.he: פרשת וישלח ממשיכה לעקוב אחרי יעקב ומשפחתו. יעקב נאבק עם איש (שלפי הפרשנות המקובלת הוא מלאך אלוהים), ובסיום המאבק האיש מעניק לו את השם ישראל. יעקב מתפייס עם אחיו עשו. דינה, בתו של יעקב, נאנסת ונשבית בידי נסיך חיווי, ואחיה הורגים את כל הזכרים בעיר ומשיבים אליהם את דינה. רחל מתה בשעת לידתו של בנימין, הצעיר בבני יעקב.

description.en: Ki Tavo (“When You Come”) opens by describing the ceremony of the first fruit offering (bikkurim) and the declaration made upon the completion of tithing. It concludes with a detailed description of blessings that follow obedience to God's laws and curses that come with their desecration.
description.he: בפרשת כי תבוא מובאות מצוות מקרא ביכורים, טקסט הודיה שנאמר בשעת הבאת הביכורים, ומצוות וידוי מעשרות, נוסח שנאמר לאחר השלמת חובת הבאת המעשרות. משה מצווה על מעמד הברכה והקללה על הר גריזים והר עיבל אחרי הכניסה לארץ ומתאר את הברכות הרבות שיחולו על בני ישראל אם ישמרו את מצוות התורה ואת הקללות והעונשים שיבואו על העם אם לא ישמרו את המצוות.

description.en: Laban is a biblical character who features in the Book of Genesis. He is the brother of Rebecca, father of Rachel and Leah, and father-in-law of Jacob. His actions are marked by trickery, as he deceptively marries Leah off to Jacob rather than Rachel, and later mistreats Jacob as an employee.

Kedoshim (“Holy”) opens by instructing the Israelites to be holy. It details dozens of laws regulating all aspects of life, including observing Shabbat, loving one’s neighbor, and leaving portions of a field for the poor. It ends by detailing punishments for certain types of idolatry and sexual misconduct.
description.he: פרשת קדושים פותחת בציווי לבני ישראל שיהיו קדושים ומפרטת עשרות דינים בתחומי פולחן וחברה, כגון שבת וקורבנות, איסור כלאיים, מצוות ואהבת לרעך כמוך, החובה להלוות לעניים ואיסור נקמה. בסוף הפרשה מפורטים עונשים בתחום איסורי עריות ועבודה זרה.

description.en: Bo (“Come”) recounts the last three plagues that God inflicts on the Egyptians: locusts, darkness, and death of firstborns. God commands the Israelites to offer a Passover lamb sacrifice. After the last plague, Pharaoh and the Egyptians demand that the Israelites leave.
description.he: בפרשת בא מסופר על שלוש המכות האחרונות שהאל מביא על מצרים. אחרי מכת הארבה נופל חושך כבד על מצרים במשך שלושה ימים. אלוהים מצווה את בני ישראל להקריב את קורבן הפסח, למרוח דם על מזוזות הבית, ולא לצאת מפתח הבית כדי להינצל ממוות. באותו לילה המשחית הורג את כל בכורות מצרים במכה האחרונה, מכת בכורות. פרעה והמצרים מגרשים את בני ישראל ממצרים.

description.en: The [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is the eighth of the ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot). When the [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) are divided into the five primary [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) – [*Keter*](/topics/keter1), [*Ḥokhma*](/topics/hokhma1), [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1), and [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) – *Hod* is encompassed in the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1) as the [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) [level](/topics/level) for the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Tiferet*](/topics/tiferet1).  *Hod* is the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) which completes the left line or column in every [*partzuf*](/topics/partzuf1) or world. Its essence is that of the fourth [level](/topics/level) ([*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1)). Because of this, and its role of completion, the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is considered female, and possessing the attribute of judgment. The name *Hod* derives from the word *hoda’ah*, thanksgiving, because the feminine (the left side) is grateful for the light that the masculine (the right side) shines on it. This light is the light of giving, which carries the light of wisdom with it, light, which was restricted as a result of the first [constriction](/topics/constriction). In the structure of the [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf), which correlates with the human body, the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of *Hod* is associated with the left thigh or leg.

Jewish folklore includes stories of the supernatural – demons, figures who defy death, otherworldly creatures – and parables, homilies, and mystical ideas. These tales are used to teach, preserve culture, and impart wisdom. Although magic is a significant element of Jewish folklore, more mundane customs and stories impart values and provide role models for desired behavior.

description.en: Sefirat HaOmer (literally, "the counting of the Omer") is the period of 49 days between Passover and Shavuot. Each day is verbally counted off. Traditionally, this period of time is a solemn one, and many avoid celebrations during this calendar period.

description.en: Vayakhel (“He Assembled”) opens as God commands the Israelites to observe the Sabbath. Moses asks for material donations for the building of the Mishkan (Tabernacle), and the people donate. A group of artisans designated by God begin building the Mishkan and its vessels.
description.he: בפרשת ויקהל בני ישראל מצווים לשמור את השבת. בני ישראל מתבקשים לתרום חומרים לבניית המשכן; הם נענים לבקשה בנדיבות ומתבקשים להפסיק לתרום. בצלאל ואהליאב מתחילים לנהל את בניית מבנה המשכן, כלי המשכן והחצר. כל פרט מבוצע כפי שציווה אלוהים את משה.

description.en: R. Chanina b. Dosa lived before and after the Temple's destruction. He was known for his piety, his faith and his ability to petition God. In this regard, the greatest scholars would turn to him to pray for them. He lived on next to nothing and experienced many miracles on behalf of himself and his family.
description.he: רבי חנינא בן דוסא חי בתקופה לפני ואחרי חורבן בית המקדש. נודע בצדקותו, באמונתו ובכוח התפילה שלו. גדולי החכמים פנו אליו וביקשו שיתפלל עבורם. הוא חי בעוני מחפיר וחווה ניסים רבים על בשרו ועל בני משפחתו.

description.en: Noach (“Noah”) begins as God decides to destroy mankind with a flood. At God’s command, the righteous Noah builds an ark, where Noah, his family, and select animals survive the flood. Noah’s children bear children, and several generations develop. God confounds the speech of people building the Tower of Babel.
description.he: פרשת נח עוסקת בהחלטה של האל להשמיד את האנושות במבול. אלוהים מצווה את נח לבנות תיבה כדי להציל את נח, את בני משפחתו ובעלי חיים. עם שוך המבול נח ומשפחתו יוצאים מן התיבה, וילדיו של נח מולידים דורות של צאצאים. אלוהים בולל את שפת האדם לאחר הניסיון לבנות את מגדל בבל. תרח עוזב את ביתו ויוצא למסע עם משפחתו, ובהם בנו אברם וכלתו שרי.

A Torah scroll (*sefer Torah* in Hebrew) is a copy of the Torah written by hand on parchment according to various rules to ensure its accuracy, readability, and holiness. It is primarily used in synagogues during Jewish prayer services.
description.he: ספר התורה הוא העתק של חמשת חומשי התורה שנכתב בידי אדם על קלף (נייר העשוי מעור בעלי חיים). כתיבת הספר חייבת להתבצע על פי כללים שנועדו לשמור על הדיוק, על הקדושה ועל קלות הקריאה של הספר. בספר התורה נעשה שימוש בבתי הכנסת בזמן התפילות, כולל בשבת.

description.en: While Judaism is often thought of as a sound-filled religion — God uses speech to utter the world into existence, and synagogues and study halls are often places of audible prayer and learning— silence has its place in the Jewish textual tradition. The high priest Aaron [reacts](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.10.3?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) to the death of his two sons with silence, and Pirkei Avot praises silence as a "[fence to wisdom](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3.13?lang=en&with=all&lang2=en)." Sources throughout the centuries discuss the place and value of silence.

The red heifer — *parah adumah* in Hebrew — is an unblemished and completely red cow that has never been put to work. The animal’s ashes are used to purify someone who has come into contact with a corpse and thereby contracted [ritual impurity](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/tumah?tab=admin).
description.he: פרה אדומה היא פרה שצבעה אדום לגמרי ללא רבב, שמעולם לא שימשה למלאכה. אפר הפרה האדומה משמש לטהר את מי שבא במגע עם אדם מת, הנקרא "טמא מת".

description.en: Doeg was an Edomite who served King Saul. He carried out the executions of a number of priests who helped David when he was fleeing Saul.
description.he: דואג, משרתו האדומי של שאול המלך, הוציא להורג כמה כוהנים שסייעו לדוד בתקופת בריחתו משאול.

description.en: Behar (“On The Mountain”) details the laws of the sabbatical year (*shemittah*), when working the land is prohibited and debts are forgiven. It also sets out laws of indentured servitude and of the jubilee year (*yovel*), when property reverts to its original ownership.
description.he: בפרשת בהר מובאים דיני שבת הארץ (שמיטה), החלה בכל שבע שנים ואסורה בה עבודת האדמה. בשנת החמישים, היא שנת היובל, נוסף על שביתה מעבודת האדמה יש לשחרר את העבדים, והקרקעות חוזרות לבעליהן המקוריים. מפורטים גם דיני מכירת קרקעות, דיני מכירת עבדים, דיני אונאת ממון ואונאת דברים, איסור ריבית ואיסורים הקשורים לעבודה זרה.

[Hallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Festivals%2C_Rosh_Chodesh%2C_Hallel%2C_Berakhah_before_the_Hallel?lang=en) consists of Psalms 113–118 and is recited on most holidays. There are, however, some holidays on which only part or none of it is recited. These chapters are psalms of thanksgiving and focus on God's communal and personal salvation for those who put their trust in God.
description.he: קריאת ההַלֵּל מורכבת מפרקים קיג-קיח בספר תהילים ונאמרת ברוב המועדים. עם זאת, ישנם מועדים שבהם נאמרים רק חלק מפרקי ההלל, ואחרים שבהם אין אומרים הלל בכלל. פרקי התהילים הכלולים בהלל הם פרקי הודיה העוסקים בגאולה ציבורית ואישית של הבוטחים בה'.

description.en: The idea that one can know God is a delicate proposition. Jewish tradition regards God as beyond comprehension, yet biblical [texts](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.55.6?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=he&with=all&lang2=he) encourage seeking God. Various Jewish texts describe ways to gain a better understanding of God and enhance knowledge of God, such as through meditation, asking philosophical questions, Torah study, or observation of the natural world.
description.he: ידיעת השם משמעה שכלול ההבנה השכלית של האדם את האלוהים והגברת המודעות לנוכחותו. יש דרכים רבות שהאדם יכול לחזק את ידיעת השם שלו, למשל מדיטציה או עיסוק בשאלות פילוסופיות.

description.en: Gehenna, or *Gehinnom* in Hebrew, is often thought of as the Jewish hell and is the term used in rabbinic literature to refer to the place where the wicked go after death. The name likely originates from a valley south of Jerusalem called Gehinnom or Gey Ben Hinnom, which the prophet Jeremiah [cursed](https://www.sefaria.org/Jeremiah.19.2?ven=Tanakh:_The_Holy_Scriptures,_published_by_JPS&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) for being a site of idolatry and child sacrifice.

Toldot (“Generations”) opens with the births of Isaac and Rebecca’s twins, Jacob and Esau. Esau sells his birthright to Jacob in exchange for soup. Isaac and Rebecca travel to Gerar, where Isaac makes a peace treaty with King Abimelech. Isaac gives Jacob the blessing meant for Esau, and Jacob runs away to his uncle Laban.
description.he: פרשת תולדות פותחת בלידת התאומים עשו ויעקב ליצחק ורבקה. עשו מוכר את בכורתו ליעקב בתמורה לנזיד עדשים. יצחק ורבקה נוסעים לגרר, ושם יצחק כורת ברית עם אבימלך מלך גרר. בעצת רבקה יעקב לובש בגדים העשויים מעורו של שעיר עיזים כדי להידמות לעשו ומבקש מאביו במרמה את ברכת הבכורה. יצחק כהה העינים נותן לו את ברכת הבכורה, ואחר כך מברך גם את עשו. יעקב בורח לבית דודו לבן מפני כעסו של אחיו עשו.

description.en: "[He put his trust in God](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.15.6?lang=bi&vside=THE_JPS_TANAKH:_Gender-Sensitive_Edition|en&with=Translation%20Open&lang2=en)," the Torah states of Abram (later to be called Abraham), as God shows him the stars and promises that one day his descendants will be so numerous that they'll be just as uncountable. This is perhaps the first moment of explicit trust in the Torah, and Abraham is often discussed as a paragon of trust in God in later Jewish texts. Many other biblical texts speak of trust in moments when help didn't feel immediately tangible, and works of Jewish thought and Musar discuss trust extensively, including its connection to knowledge of God, the balance between trust and action, and how to practically develop and grow one's trust.

description.en: Tetzaveh (“You Shall Command”) opens as God instructs Moses to appoint Aaron and his sons as priests. God details how to make the priestly clothing, how to sanctify the priests and offer sacrifices during the seven days of inauguration in the Mishkan (Tabernacle), and how to build the golden altar.
description.he: פרשת תצוה עוסקת בבגדי הכהונה לאהרן, הכהן הגדול, ולבניו הכהנים, שישמשו במשכן. הכהנים יוקדשו לעבודה במשכן על ידי סדרה של קורבנות שיוקרבו בשבעת ימי המילואים. משה מצווה על קורבן התמיד, הקרב בכל יום על המזבח בפתח המשכן. כמו כן מתואר מזבח הזהב שמוצב בתוך המשכן, ועליו מקטירים את קטורת הסמים.

description.en: The synagogue (beit knesset, meaning “house of assembly”) serves as a spiritual center for Jewish communities around the world. Because of their role as houses of prayer, there are many laws about how synagogues should be built, as well as what is allowed in and around them.

description.en: Jewish textual tradition values giving and [generosity](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/generosity?tab=admin). The Torah instructs providing for those in need and requires the distribution of agricultural gifts to the poor, the priests, and the Levites. Later Jewish texts elaborate on these commandments and on the importance of supporting communal institutions.

description.en: The sun plays a central role in Jewish texts as a physical source of light, a regulator of ritual time, and a symbol of radiance, strength, and divine order. In the Bible, it is created on the fourth day of creation and features in key narratives such as Joseph's [dream](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.37.9?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) and the miracle of Joshua halting the sun, as well as in poetic [metaphors](https://www.sefaria.org/Judges.5.31?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Rabbinic literature ties practices like daily prayer to sunrise and sunset and discusses the sun's role in structuring the calendar. Liturgical [texts](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Sefard%2C_Shabbat_Morning_Services%2C_Shema_%26_Blessings.4?ven=hebrew|Torat_Emet_357&lang=bi) praise God for continually renewing creation and bringing forth the sun each day, and Jewish philosophical works develop the sun as a symbol of divine constancy.

description.en: Vaera (“I Appeared”) opens as God promises to redeem the enslaved Israelites and bring them to the Promised Land. When Pharaoh repeatedly refuses to let the Israelites go, God sends a series of plagues: water turning to blood, frogs, lice, wild animals, death of livestock, boils, and hail.
description.he: פרשת וארא נפתחת בהבטחת האל להוציא את בני ישראל ממצרים ולהביאם לארץ זבת חלב ודבש. משה דורש מפרעה לשלוח את בני ישראל ממצרים, אך פרעה מסרב שוב ושוב. אלוהים מביא מכות על מצרים בכל פעם שפרעה מסרב: מים הופכים לדם, מכת צפרדעים, כינים, ערוב, דבר, שחין וברד.

description.en: In Tzav (“Command”), God tells Moses about the sacrifices offered in the Tabernacle (portable sanctuary), including a meal offering brought by the high priest, guilt offerings, and offerings of thanks. Moses initiates Aaron and Aaron’s sons for priestly service in the Tabernacle.
description.he: בפרשת צו מתוארים קורבן עולה, שכל חלקיו (מלבד העור) נשרפים כליל על המזבח; קורבן מנחה, שהוא קורבן מן הצומח; וכן קורבנות חטאת, אשם, שלמים ותודה. נאסר על בני ישראל לאכול דם וחלב – חלקים מן הבהמה המוקרבים תמיד על המזבח. משה מקדיש את אהרן ובניו לכהונה בסדרת קורבנות המובאים בשבעת ימי המילואים.

description.en: Artistic representation is a noticeable part of many contemporary Jewish spaces — from synagogue stain glass windows to artistic ritual items like menorahs, mezuzot, and more. The value of intricate design and artistic expression can be traced back to the Bible, which features detailed accounts of the building of the Tabernacle and its vessels, and later, the Temple. Rabbinic sources discuss the concept of *hiddur mitzvah*, or beautifying the commandments, in part by investing in beautiful ritual objects. Other sources describe the pursuit of beauty as frivolous and [vain](https://www.sefaria.org/Proverbs.31.30?lang=bi), and some [biblical](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.20.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) [prohibitions](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.4.16?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) have traditionally been understood as cautioning against creating visual images.

description.en: Conversion refers to the process through which non-Jews may become Jewish. The concept is often associated with the biblical character [Ruth](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/ruth), a woman of Moabite origin who is described as "[taking refuge](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth.2.12?ven=The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=bi) under the wings of God's presence." Rabbinic sources see this as an indicator of Ruth's conversion and interpret details about the laws of conversion from Ruth's story.
description.he: גיור הוא תהליך שבו לא-יהודים יכולים להפוך ליהודים. המושג מקושר לעתים קרובות לדמותה המקראית של רות, אישה מואבית שהצטרפה לעם ישראל. תהליך הגיור כולל מעמד של קבלת המצוות, טבילה במקווה ולזכרים גם ברית מילה.

description.en: [Birkat HaMazon](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Berachot%2C_Birkat_HaMazon?lang=bi), known in English as "Grace After Meals" is the series of four blessings recited after a meal in which has eaten bread. While all other blessings are commanded by the rabbis, proclaiming thanks to God after a meal is a commandment from the Torah itself, in [Deuteronomy 8:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.8.10?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).
description.he: ברכת המזון היא סדרה של ארבע ברכות הנאמרות אחרי סעודה שבה נאכל לחם. זו הברכה היחידה שאמירתה היא מצווה מן התורה (דברים ח, י) ולא מדברי חכמים.

description.en: The Jewish people are often called "the people of the Book." While "the Book" in the phrase at hand refers to the Tanakh, the phrase also reflects the centrality of books and the [study of Jewish texts](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/torah-study?tab=admin) in Judaism. Within traditional Jewish literature, much is written on the value and nature of books: Halakhic texts discuss how to treat sacred books, rabbinic texts explore the authorship of different biblical books, and works of Jewish thought and Kabbalah consider the impact of text study on the mind and soul.

description.en: The snake appears from the opening narratives of the Torah, as a snake [entices](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.1?lang=bi&aliyot=0) Eve to eat from the tree of knowledge. Various other biblical verses mention snakes as part of stories, prophecies, and metaphors. Rabbinic texts discuss the dangerous nature of the snake and different laws surrounding snakes, like the [permissibility](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.121b.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) of killing them on Shabbat.

description.en: Cases and discussion of ethics abound throughout the Jewish textual tradition, as texts aim to instruct and analyze how to live a life of moral principles.

The [priestly blessing](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Weekday%2C_Shacharit%2C_Amidah%2C_Birkat_Kohanim.1?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) — birkat kohanim in Hebrew —  is a blessing recited by kohanim (those of priestly descent) unto the congregation. Its origins are in [Numbers 6:24–27](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.6.24?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), and these verses are the blessing itself. In Israel, the blessing is recited as part of daily service. Outside of Israel, customs vary as to when it is recited.
description.he: ברכת כהנים היא ברכה הנאמרת על ידי הכהנים אל בני ישראל. הציווי על הברכה כתוב בספר במדבר והיא כוללת שלושה פסוקים ומכאן הכינוי הנוסף לברכה: 'ברכה משולשת'. כיום, הכהנים מברכים את הברכה בכל יום בתפילת שחרית ובתפילת מוסף במהלך חזרת הש"ץ. בקהילות רבות בחוץ לארץ ברכת כהנים נאמרת רק בתפילות החגים.

description.en: See section 83, where it is explained that spiritual beings are separated and divided from one another by their difference of form. Know that divergent forms, from one extreme to the other, separates these beings and distances them from one extreme to its opposite, until there is no suckling between them at all. As you already know, the supernal light contains only a will to give, not to receive anything, whereas the kelippot have the exact opposite forms: Only a will to receive and to swallow everything; they have no will to give whatsoever. Therefore, they are separated from the Source of Life and are called dead, they and all that cleave to them. This must be understood (Talmud Eser Sefirot, v. 3, Q & A 88).

description.en: Jehoiakim was the 18th king of Judah. Originally an Egyptian vassal, he switched allegiance to Babylonia in the hopes of preventing Babylon from destroying Jerusalem. In rabbinic literature, he is portrayed as a very wicked king.
description.he: יהויקים היה המלך השמונה־עשר של יהודה. בתחילה היה כפוף לממלכת מצרים אך לאחר מכן הכריז על נאמנותו לבבל בתקווה למנוע את חורבן ירושלים. בספרות חז"ל מתואר כמלך רשע.

description.en: The *sanhedrin* ("assembly") was a legislative and judicial assembly of either 23 or 70 elders, existing at both a local and central level in the ancient Land of Israel.

description.en: Incense (Ketoret) was offered daily on the Golden Altar in the Mishkan and Temple, and its ingredients are dictated in the Torah. There are also mystical properties associated with it, as seen from its use in protecting Jews from God's wrath in the desert (Num. 17).
description.he: בכל יום התבצעה הקטרת (שרֵפת) קטורת על מזבח הזהב במשכן ובמקדש. מרכיבי הקטורת נזכרים בתורה. בקטורת נקשרו תכונות מיסטיות מסוימות, כפי שעולה מהשימוש בה בהגנה על בני ישראל מפני מגפה שהביא עליהם אלוהים (במדבר יז).

description.en: Bread is considered a staple of life in the Jewish textual tradition. Biblical figures offer bread to their guests as a marker of hospitality, and the sacred showbread plays a role in the rituals of the Tabernacle and Temple. [Many laws](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Challah.1.6.3?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) govern the preparation, baking, and consumption of bread. Bread is unique in that its consumption necessitates reciting the full [Birkat HaMazon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/birkat-hamazon?tab=admin) (Grace After Meals).
description.he: הלחם נחשב למצרך יסוד במטבח העם היהודי. הלכות רבות מתארות כיצד יש להכינו ולאוכלו, וכן הוא המזון היחיד שאכילתו מחייבת ברכה מלאה אחריה (ברכת המזון).

description.en: Shimon the Righteous was a high priest and teacher at a time of political flux in the region. He is credited with meeting Alexander the Great and convincing him not to attack Jerusalem. He was the first teacher mentioned in Pirkei Avot and among the last surviving members of the Great Assembly, a Rabbinic legislative body that existed in the Second Temple period .
description.he: שמעון היה כוהן גדול בתקופה של תמורות פוליטיות באזור. מסופר שהוא נפגש עם אלכסנדר הגדול ושכנע אותו להימנע מהתקפת ירושלים. הוא החכם הראשון המוזכר בפרקי אבות ומאחרוני שיירי כנסת הגדולה, גוף מחוקק של חכמים מתקופת הבית השני.

description.en: Sleep features from the outset of the Bible, as God [casts](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.2.21?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) a deep sleep on Adam when God creates Eve. Other biblical texts incorporate sleep as well – as a [step](https://www.sefaria.org/Judges.4.21?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) in a plot, as a metaphor for laziness or spiritual disengagement, or as a [precursor](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.12?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) to divinely-inspired dreams. Rabbinic and kabbalistic texts later discuss the spiritual significance of sleep and dreams, as well as halakhic questions related to sleep, such as the parameters for the obligation to sleep in the sukkah. Jewish liturgy incorporates prayers to be recited upon going to sleep and upon waking up in the morning.

description.en: Upon placing the first human in the [garden of Eden](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/garden-of-eden?tab=sources), God immediately commands him not to eat from the [tree of knowledge of good and evil](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-tree-of-knowledge?tab=sources), lest he die. Several verses later, in [Genesis 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.3.1?lang=bi&with=Rashi&lang2=en), after God has created [Adam's](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam?tab=sources) counterpart, [Eve](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/eve?tab=sources), a [snake](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/snakes1?tab=sources) convinces her to partake of the forbidden fruit, which she in turn shares with Adam. And while Adam, Eve, and the snake are not punished with death, they are punished.

description.en: The ten [*sefirot*](/topics/sefirot) that are one below the other, which result from the ascent of the [*Malkhut*](/topics/malkhut1) to the Creator, are called [*partzufim*](/topics/partzuf) (as stated in *Histaklut Penimit* 8:13, section 1) (*Talmud Eser Sefirot*, v. 3, Q & A 83).

The mikveh is a pool (literally, a “gathering”) of water from a natural source. While the Temples stood, to gain entry into the Temple, to partake of certain sacrifices, or for a couple to be intimate — among other reasons — Jews tried to maintain a status of ritual purity. While there are different kinds of ritual impurity and as many processes to regain a status of ritual purity, immersion in a mikveh, a ritual bath, is an important element in the purification process. Today, the practice of immersion in a mikveh is used to mark life transitions, conversion to Judaism, to ready oneself for Yom Kippur, before birth, and as a central element in the observance of the laws of niddah (the practices surrounding menstruation, intimacy, and ritual purity).

description.en: Rosh Chodesh (the new month)  is celebrated for either one or two days. Before the calendar was set, this was determined by whether the new moon was seen on the 30th of the month. The Torah instituted that each new month be commemorated with a sacrifice. While no animals are currently sacrificed, many mark Rosh Chodesh with extra singing and prayers, including [Hallel](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/hallel?tab=sources), [Torah reading](https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.28?lang=bi&aliyot=0), and a [haftarah](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.66?lang=bi). In some communities, women gather together and refrain from work in honor of the womens' refusal to contribute to the making of the golden calf.

enBio.value: Moshe ben Nachman, also known as Ramban, was a leading Torah scholar of the middle ages who authored commentaries on Torah and the Talmud. He was a posek who wrote responsa and stand-alone works on Halachic topics, as well as works on mysticism, science and philosophy. Ramban's commentary on the Torah often critiques earlier commentaries and incorporates kabbalistic teachings. He was born in Gerona, Spain, where he established a large yeshiva which produced hundreds of disciples who became leaders of Spanish Jewry. In 1263 he took part in a debate in Barcelona with an apostate Jew named Pablo Christiani, at the behest of the Church. In 1267, at the age of 72, he immigrated to the Holy Land, where he settled in Akko (Acre). He died there at age 76.

description.en: Naomi is one of the chief figures of the Book of Ruth. She was Ruth's mother-in-law who moved to Moab with her family during a famine, only to return to her home in Bethlehem with Ruth after her husband and sons died. Despondent and poor, she found hope again when Ruth married Boaz and bore a son.
description.he: נעמי, אחת הדמויות המרכזיות במגילת רות, הייתה חמותה של רות. היא עזבה את בית לחם עם משפחתה בעקבות רעב ששרר בארץ והתיישבה במואב. לאחר שמתו בעלה ובניה, שבה עם רות לביתה בבית לחם ענייה וחסרת כול. תקוותה שבה אליה כשרות התחתנה עם בועז וילדה לו בן.

description.en: Eve was the first woman, the "mother of all," created by being separated from [Adam's](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/adam?tab=sources) body. In the [garden of Eden](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/garden-of-eden?tab=sources), the snake convinced Eve to try the forbidden fruit of the [tree of knowledge](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-tree-of-knowledge?tab=sources), from which she also gave to Adam. The result was that they were both expelled from the garden and that she and all of womankind would be cursed to endure difficult [childbirths](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/birth?tab=sources) even as they desire their husbands, to whom they are subject.
description.he: חוה היא האישה הראשונה מבנות מינה ואם כל חי. היא נוצרה מצלעו של אדם והופרדה ממנו. הנחש בגן עדן שכנע אותה לטעום מפרי עץ הדעת, וממנו האכילה גם את אדם. בעקבות זאת גורשו שניהם מגן עדן, ובנות מינה קוללו בלידות קשות ובשיעבוד לגברים.

Acharei Mot (“After The Death”) opens by describing the ritual service of Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement. It then details the prohibitions of offering sacrifices outside of the Tabernacle and of eating animal blood and ends with a list of forbidden sexual relations.
description.he: פרשת אחרי מות פותחת בפירוט סדר עבודת יום הכיפורים במשכן: נוסף על קורבנות מיוחדים ועל עבודת הקטורת, עבודת הכהן הגדול כוללת הטלת גורלות לשני שעירי החטאת: אחד מהם מוקרב על גבי המזבח, והאחר - השעיר לעזאזל - נושא את עוונות בני ישראל ונשלח למדבר. הפרשה ממשיכה באיסור לשחוט מחוץ למשכן, באיסור להקריב קורבנות מחוץ למשכן, באיסור אכילת דם, בחובת כיסוי הדם בעוף ובחיה ובטומאת נבלה וטרפה. הפרשה מסתיימת ברשימת איסורי עריות.

From the outset of the Torah, its characters are challenged to take responsibility for their actions: God questions Adam and Eve about their sin in the Garden of Eden and later asks their son Cain about the whereabouts of the brother whom he murdered. Responsibility is a foundation of the covenantal pact between God and the Israelites that appears throughout the Bible. The concept that [all Jews are responsible for one another](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra%2C_Bechukotai%2C_Chapter_7.5?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) reverberates throughout Jewish texts, as they delve into the practical applications of responsibility and its theoretical underpinnings.

Dogs first feature in the Torah in the book of Exodus, when, during the final plague in Egypt, [God ensures](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.11.7?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) that not even a dog would snarl at the people of Israel. Later in the same book, the Torah instructs that certain meat that is forbidden for human consumption be [given to dogs](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.22.30?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Rabbinic sources explore the connection between these two references to canines. In other biblical, rabbinic, halakhic, and mystical texts, dogs feature in many negative contexts — for example, they are often depicted as feeding on corpses and as dangerous to humans. Still, other sources highlight positive qualities of dogs, such as their ability to sense the unseen and their helpfulness to people who need it.

description.en: Music has played a role in Judaism since biblical times: the people of Israel sang and danced as they crossed the Red Sea, David played the harp to calm King Saul, and the book of Psalms consists of 150 poems, some of which describe calling to God [through music](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.144.9?lang=he&with=all&lang2=he). Rabbinic literature describes the songs the Levites sang in the Temple and discusses halakhic questions relating to music. Music is a central part of contemporary Jewish life for many, from the tunes associated with liturgical texts, the chanting of the weekly Torah portion, and Jewish songs sung on Shabbat and other occasions.

description.en: The world of *Beria* is the second of the four worlds (after the supernal world of *Adam Kadmon*) that emanate and descend from another in the process of creation. According to one explanation, its name is derived from the Hebrew word *bar*, a term that connotes that which is external, implying that the world of *Beria* is a garment for the world of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut). The world of *Beria* parallels the [*sefira*](/topics/sefira2) of [*Bina*](/topics/bina3), or the second [level](/topics/level) of creation, and it is the beginning point of the [enclothing](/topics/enclothe) of [*Atzilut*](/topics/atzilut) into a reality that created beings can receive. The world of *Beria* is also called the world of the throne, signifying the Divine lowering itself onto a throne, so to speak, to interact with its creations and the beginning of the revelation of the Divine to lower [levels](/topics/level) of existence. It is also known as the world of souls, since the created entities called souls begin to have significance as receivers of the supernal light. The angelic entities that exist in this world are called *serafim*.

Power is often understood as a demonstrable, physical strength. However, an inner power of restraint is also seen as a sign of strength of character. The Jewish textual tradition frequently regards God as all-powerful, and this divine power is contrasted with the lesser power of mere mortals. The power expressed through ongoing creation, nature, and the world is presented in various genres as an emanation of God’s power.

description.en: Belief in the coming of the Messiah and the messianic era has been a principle of faith for the Jewish people throughout the Jewish textual tradition. Liturgy includes yearning for the messianic era, and prophets and later commentaries and texts explore what that era will look like. Some describe the era as cosmic in nature with supernatural elements, while others view it as more limited in scope and focus on rational outcomes. In all of these, however, exists a hope for a better future.

Written texts play a central role in Jewish tradition. The means of the composition and transmission of texts has varied through Jewish history as different technologies have become available — from carved stone tablets and memorized oral traditions to hand-copied manuscripts to printed books to digital resources. Even with adaptations to new technologies, the ancient scribal practice of hand-writing Torah scrolls continues until today, with particular materials and practices required by law and custom. Works such as the [Mishnah](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Mishnah) and the [Talmud](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Talmud) are considered to be in the category of [Oral Torah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/oral-torah?tab=notable-sources), even though they have long ago been written down, in contrast to the Written Torah, which is limited to the [Hebrew Bible](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Tanakh). The act of writing is one of the basic labors forbidden on [Shabbat](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shabbat?tab=notable-sources) and major [festivals](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/yom-tov?tab=notable-sources).

description.en: Hope is a defining theme of Jewish textual tradition. God’s [promises](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.15.5?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) to Abraham and Sarah, and to later patriarchs and matriarchs, inspired faith in a future that could not yet be seen, while the people of Israel's [redemption](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-exodus-from-egypt?tab=admin) from Egypt demonstrated that deep suffering can give way to freedom. During times of destruction and exile, prophets such as Jeremiah and Ezekiel sustained the people with visions of return, renewal, and restoration. This enduring hope continues to shape Jewish life today, finding expression in daily prayers for redemption and the declaration, often recited at the Passover seder, of “next year in Jerusalem.”

R. Pinchas was the son-in-law of R. Shimon bar Yochai and lived during the time of R. Yehudah haNasi. He was most famous for his outstanding piety, especially in the area of tithes, such that even his donkey was stringent about them. He is also well known for his ladder of virtues, later immortalized by R. Moshe Hayyim Luzzatto.
description.he: רבי פנחס היה חתנו של רבי שמעון בר יוחאי וחי בתקופתו של רבי יהודה הנשיא. נודע באדיקותו בייחוד בתחום המעשרות, ומסופר שאפילו חמורו היה מחמיר בהן. לימים הונצחה חסידתו הגדולה על ידי רבי משה חיים לוצאטו בספרו מסילת ישרים.

description.en: [Song of Songs](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs?tab=contents) (“Shir Hashirim”) is one of the five megillot (scrolls), part of the section of the Hebrew Bible called Writings. Attributed in its opening verse to [King Solomon](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/king-solomon?tab=sources), the book records poetic conversations between two lovers, describing their pursuit of each other through vineyards and fields of blossoming flowers. It is traditionally understood as a metaphor for the loving relationship between God and the people of Israel, and is often read publicly on Passover or on Shabbat evening.

description.en: In Nitzavim (“Standing”), Moses addresses the Israelites, emphasizing the importance of following God’s covenant and of not worshiping other gods. description.he: בפרשת נצבים משה פונה לכל חלקי העם, ממנהיגי העם ועד חוטבי העצים ושואבי המים, וכולל אותם בברית עם אלוהים. משה מדגיש את העונשים הצפויים לעוברים על הברית. הוא מתאר את תהליך התשובה הצפוי לעם ישראל בגלות ומתאר את שמירת מצוות האל כדבר אפשרי ובהישג יד: "לא בשמים היא."

description.en: Located between Israel and Egypt, Midian was inhabited by the descendents of Midian, who was a son of Abraham. Moses spent his exile from Egypt in Midian and married a Midianite woman. Later, Israel was persecuted by Midian on the final legs of their journey to Israel.

description.en: In Jewish tradition, having a home means that one has a place in which to fulfill such obligations as [welcoming guests](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/welcoming-guests?sort=Relevance&tab=notable-sources), placing [mezuzot](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mezuzah?tab=notable-sources) on their doorposts, and commemorating the [destruction of the Temples](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/destruction-of-the-temple?tab=notable-sources). Jewish tradition also uses the idea of home as a metaphor, likening a wife to a home and imagining God as dwelling in God’s homes of the [Tabernacle](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=notable-sources) and, later, the [Temples](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/beit-hamikdash?tab=notable-sources). Peace in one's home ([shalom bayit](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shalom-bayit?tab=notable-sources)) is also a priority.

description.en: As the nation responsible for the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem, Rome has a prominent place in the Jewish literature. Although most sources are critical of the pride and viciousness of the Roman Empire, some sources are more apologetic about Rome.

description.en: In the Torah, the first commandment given to Adam and Eve is to "[be fruitful and multiply](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.1.28?ven=english|The_Koren_Jerusalem_Bible&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en)," understood in rabbinic literature as an obligation to bear children and continue the process of creation. Children occupy a central place in Jewish tradition, symbolizing both the continuity of the Jewish people and the transmission of Torah from one generation to the next. The Torah repeatedly emphasizes the responsibility of parents to [teach](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.6.7?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) their children God's commandments, and rabbinic sources understand that the world’s very [future](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishneh_Torah%2C_Torah_Study.2.1?ven=hebrew|Torat_Emet_363&lang=bi) depends on the pure words spoken by young children learning Torah. Texts throughout the Jewish textual tradition explore how to educate children, responsibilities of parents and communities toward their children, and what it looks like to [yearn](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/infertility?tab=admin) for children.
description.he: מקורות יהדות רבים מדגישים את חשיבות הולדת הילדים וגידולם. הילדים נתפסים כברכה וכהמשכיות של עם ישראל. חובת ההולדה נובעת מהמצווה "פרו ורבו", והיא אחת המצוות הראשונות בתורה. חכמים ראו בלימוד תורה לילדים ערך עליון ואף דרשו שעתיד העולם תלוי בהבל פיהם של תינוקות של בית רבן. גידול הילדים כרוך באחריות לחנכם לערכים, למצוות ולדרך ארץ, וזאת מתוך אהבה, הדרכה ודוגמה אישית.

description.en: Though the Torah gives few procedural details, under certain circumstances, it does allow for divorce. The laws of divorce are developed in detail throughout the rabbinic period and in later halakhic literature. To this day, rabbis and Jewish leaders continue to grapple with the intricacies and consequences of these laws. And in that marriage is an oft-used metaphor for the relationship between God and the Jewish people, so too does divorce appear as an oft-rejected possibility.
description.he: התורה מתארת אפשרות של גירושין על ידי מתן 'ספר כריתות' של האיש לאישה הידוע בשפה ההלכתית כ'גט'. הלכות הגירושין פותחו באופן מפורט על ידי חז"ל ובהמשך על ידי חכמי הראשונים והאחרונים. עד היום מנהיגי קהילות יהודיים ממשיכים להתמודד עם מורכבותן של הלכות אלה. קשר נישואין הוא מטאפורה ליחסים בין אלוהים לעם ישראל, כך גם הגירושין במצב של משבר וחורבן וגם התיקון והאיחוי שלהם.

description.en: The Torah instructs treating laborers justly, forbidding [delaying](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.19.13?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) their payment and – according to [rabbinic understanding](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.87a.19?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) – instructing that they may eat from the produce they harvest. Various rabbinic sources discuss the value of labor and the honor it gives to one who does it, as well as responsibilities of employers toward their workers and workers toward their employees.

description.en: Devarim (“Words”) is the first Torah portion in the Book of Deuteronomy, the final book of the Torah. In it, Moses recounts events from the Israelites’ travels in the desert, like the appointment of judges, the sin of the spies, and the wars with the Emorite kings Sihon and Og.
description.he: דברים היא הפרשה הראשונה בספר דברים, החומש החמישי והאחרון בתורה. בספר מובאים נאומי משה, שבהם הוא מזכיר אירועים מהעבר, סוקר מצוות שכבר ניתנו ומצווה מצוות חדשות. בפרשה משה מספר על הצורך במינוי שופטים להנהגת העם. הוא גם מזכיר את חטא המרגלים, שבו התלונן העם על הכניסה העתידית לארץ כנען, את העונש שהוטל על העם לנדוד במדבר ארבעים שנה ואת מלחמות ישראל במדבר.

enBio.value: Avraham ben Meir ibn Ezra, better known simply as Ibn Ezra, was a medieval Spanish Torah commentator, poet, philosopher and grammarian. While he wrote on grammar, philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and mathematics, he is most famous for his Biblical commentaries, which, alongside those of Rashi, are ubiquitous and indispensable. His commentaries focus on grammatical explanations and the "peshat" (plain-sense) meaning of the text. He often incorporates biting or humorous comments directed toward other commentators, especially towards the Karaites. He maintained a deep friendship with R. Yehudah Halevi, and quotes some of his interpretations in his commentaries. His poetry is still read and sung as part of the regular liturgy. Ibn Ezra knew great poverty and traveled widely, almost incessantly, teaching and making connections with fellow scholars, notably Rabbenu Tam in France.

description.en: Avraham ben Meir ibn Ezra, better known simply as Ibn Ezra, was a medieval Spanish Torah commentator, poet, philosopher, and grammarian. A polymath, he wrote on grammar, philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and mathematics. He is most famous for his biblical commentaries, which, alongside those of Rashi, are ubiquitous and indispensable. His commentaries focus on rational, grammatical explanations and the *peshat* (plain sense) meaning of the text. He is often critical of other commentators and especially of Karaites, a group of Jews who rejected the Oral Torah and rabbinic teachings. He maintained a deep friendship with the contemporary Spanish philosopher, [Judah Halevi](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/yehuda-halevi?tab=popular-writing-of), and quotes some of his interpretations in his commentaries. His poetry is still read and sung as part of the regular liturgy. Ibn Ezra knew great poverty and traveled widely, almost incessantly, teaching and making connections with fellow scholars, notably Rabbenu Tam in France.

description.en: Welcoming guests — *hachnasat orchim* in Hebrew — is considered an act of loving-kindness and a commandment in Judaism, described as greater than [greeting the divine presence](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.127a.13?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Modeled most prominently by the biblical character [Abraham](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/abraham?sort=Relevance&tab=notable-sources), welcoming guests can involve housing them, feeding them, and making them feel comfortable.
description.he: הכנסת אורחים היא רכיב חשוב בתוך המצווה הכללית של גמילות חסדים. מלבד פתיחת הבית לאורח, הכנסת אורחים כוללת לינה ומזון, כל זאת מתוך אהבה ובסבר פנים יפות.

description.en: Though the contemporary Hebrew word for imagination, *dimyon*, is not found in the Torah, the first book of the Torah speaks of "[thoughts of the heart](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.6.5?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en)," and characters throughout the Bible employ imaginative thinking to [build](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.11.3?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en), [protect](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.12.13?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), [create](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.31.4?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), and [develop schemes](https://www.sefaria.org/II_Samuel.14.2?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Later sources discuss the use of imagination in prayer, its role in prophecy and everyday life, and its use as a tool in parenting.

Rabban Gamliel became Nasi soon after Hillel died, shortly before the Temple's destruction. Part of his tenure came during a short respite from the Jews' troubles with the reign of Agrippa, who was befriended and taught by R. Gamliel. Many leniencies were legislated under him, and it is was likely he who brought the Great Academy of Jerusalem to Yavneh.
description.he: רבן גמליאל התמנה לנשיא זמן קצר אחרי מות הלל וסמוך לחורבן בית המקדש. בחלק מתקופת כהונתו זכו היהודים להפוגה מבעיות עם השלטון, לאחר שאגריפס, מלך יהודה התיידד עם רבן גמליאל ולמד אצלו. תחת ידו יצאו הקלות רבות בהלכה, והוא ככל הנראה היה האחראי להעברת הסנהדרין מירושלים ליבנה.

description.en: Oil features in various contexts in the Jewish textual tradition. In the Bible, oil is used to anoint kings, High Priests, and vessels of the [Tabernacle (mishkan)](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mishkan?tab=sources), as fuel for the [Menorah](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/menorah1?tab=sources), and in various biblical stories. Oil also features as an element in food, cosmetics, medicine, and sacrifices, among other functions.
description.he: ברוב המקרים השמן המוזכר בתנ"ך הוא שמן צמחי, ובייחוד כזה המופק מזיתים. השמן מילא תפקיד בפעולות רבות במסורת היהודית, אך השימוש העיקרי בו היה חומר בעֵרה למנורה שבבית המקדש.

description.en: Zevulun was the tenth son of Jacob and the sixth with his wife Leah. He was the founder of the Tribe of Zevulun.

description.en: Jewish tradition, with roots in midrash, maintains that Israelites stood at [Mount Sinai](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/mount-sinai?tab=admin) as though they were “one person with one heart.” [Acheinu](https://www.sefaria.org/Siddur_Ashkenaz%2C_Weekday%2C_Shacharit%2C_Torah_Reading%2C_Reading_from_Sefer%2C_Raising_the_Torah.9?ven=hebrew|The_Metsudah_siddur,_1981&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en), a prayer expressing Jewish unity, occupies an important place for many in Jewish prayer. The Torah also warns of the dangers of uniformity, through stories like the [Tower of Babel](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/tower-of-babel?tab=admin), and Jewish texts throughout the ages consider how to balance unity with values that at times conflict with it.

description.en: Chametz refers to leavened [bread](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/bread?tab=sources), understood by the rabbis to be any food containing one of five species of grain — wheat, barley, oat, spelt and rye — that has been allowed to rise. Several biblical verses command that one abstain from consuming chametz on the Passover holiday and to avoid encountering it in other ways.
description.he: חמץ הוא קמח של אחד ממיני הדגן שבא במגע עם מים, וכתוצאה מכך הפך לבצק ותפח. מצווה מרכזית בחג הפסח היא להימנע מאכילת חמץ במשך שבעה ימים, בנוסף למצוות אכילת מצה בליל הסדר. סיבה מרכזית למצוות אלו היא המסורת שבמהלך יציאת מצרים, לחמם של בני ישראל לא הספיק להחמיץ ולתפוח.

description.en: R. Simlai first moved from Babylonia to Lud, but later moved to the Sanhedrin's seat in the Galilee, where he became an important scholar in Rabbi's court. He is known for his debates with Christians, as well as for his homiletical teachings.
description.he: רבי שמלאי עלה מבבל לארץ ישראל והתיישב בלוד, אך מאוחר יותר עבר לגליל, שימש שם כחבר בסנהדרין והיה לחכם חשוב בחצרו של רבי יהודה הנשיא. נודע בפולמוסים שקיים עם הנוצרים ובדרשותיו.

description.en: Rabbi Mana (I) was a student of Rabbi Yannai and an influential teacher at the time of R. Yochanan.
description.he: רבי מנא (הראשון), תלמידו של רבי ינאי, היה רב בעל השפעה בדורו של רבי יוחנן.

description.en: Nachshon ben Aminadav was a biblical figure, who served as a leader of the tribe of Judah. He was the brother of Elisheva, the wife of Aaron the Priest. He is known primarily for an act described in rabbinic literature, in which he was the first to jump into the Red Sea as the people of Israel escaped their enslavement in Egypt, prompting God to split the sea. In the wake of that story, Nachshon is often used as  a symbol of initiative and courage.
description.he: נחשון בן עמינדב היה גיסו של אהרן הכהן, ושימש כנשיא שבט יהודה בתקופת שהייתם של בני ישראל במדבר. נחשון נודע בעיקר בגלל המדרש המתאר את אומץ לבו לקפוץ ראשון למי ים סוף בזמן קריעת ים סוף. כתוצאה מכך, נחשון נחשב לסמל של ההשתדלות אותה האדם צריך לעשות בנוסף לבטחונו באל.

description.en: Kabbalat Shabbat (Welcoming the Shabbat) is a service developed by the Kabbalists of Safed in the 16th century. It is composed primarily of Psalms, but includes other elements. These include the famous hymn, Lecha Dodi (Come, my beloved), which was written there at that time.
description.he: קבלת שבת היא תפילה שפותחה על ידי מקובלי צפת במאה השש־עשרה. התפילה מורכבת בעיקר מפרקי תהילים, אך היא כוללת גם מרכיבים נוספים, בהם הפיוט הנודע "לכה דודי" שנכתב בתקופה זו.

description.en: The daughters of Tzelofchad were the only children of the biblical character Tzelofchad. As only men were allowed to inherit their fathers' land, the daughters were concerned that Tzelofchad's land would leave their family. They petitioned Moses, and God responded that if a man had no sons, daughters could inherit his land.
description.he: לצלפחד היו חמש בנות, ולא היו לו בנים. הואיל ורק גברים יכלו לרשת את נחלת אבי המשפחה, בנות צלפחד חששו שנחלת אביהן תנושל ממשפחתן. הן ביקשו ממשה שיאפשר להן לרשת את הנחלה, האל נענה להן, ובעקבות בקשתן קבע שאם לאדם אין בנים, בנותיו יכולות לרשת את נחלתו.

description.en: The Lulav is a closed palm frond shaken on Sukkot alongside willow (arava) and myrtle (hadas) branches, as well as with a citron (etrog). Although the word Lulav technically only means “palm branch,” it’s usually used to refer to all of the branches and sometimes the citron as well.
description.he: הלולב הוא ניצן סגור של עלה דקל, אחד מארבעת המינים של חג הסוכות. את הלולב מנענעים בסוכות יחד עם אתרוג וענפי ערבה והדס. אף שהמשמעות המילולית של המילה "לולב" היא ענף דקל, לרוב כאשר מדברים על הלולב מתכוונים גם להדס ולערבה ולפעמים אף לאתרוג.

description.en: The jubilee (yovel) year is the 50th year in the biblical agricultural cycle and occurs after seven cycles of seven-year shemittah cycles. During the jubilee year, [a shofar is blown on Yom Kippur](https://www.sefaria.org/Leviticus.25.9?ven=The_Contemporary_Torah,_Jewish_Publication_Society,_2006&lang=he&with=all&lang2=he), land ownership resets to its original holders, and all Israelite slaves are set free. Like the [shemittah (sabbatical year)](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shemitah?tab=sources) year, the jubilee year is one in which the land is not worked.

description.en: Through the Torah's commandments and the prophets' voices, God demands that the Jewish people behave with justice and righteousness. These imperatives are taken up by the ancient rabbis and later Jewish thinkers who endeavor to further define what justice is, what it requires of us, and to imagine what a just world might look like, or if that will only come to be in a messianic age.

In Ha’azinu (“Listen”) , Moses recites a poem praising God and criticizing the sins of the Israelites. He describes the misfortunes that the Israelites will face and the damage God will ultimately wreak on their oppressors. The portion ends as God commands Moses to ascend Mount Nebo, where he is to die.
description.he: בפרשת האזינו מובאת שירה שמשבחת את אלוהים ומבקרת את העבירות העתידיות של בני ישראל. בשירה מתוארים הסבל והצרות שיבואו על העם וכן העונשים העתידים לבוא על אויבי עם ישראל. הפרשה מסתיימת בציווי על משה לעלות להר נבו, שבו ימות.

description.en: A mezuzah is the small parchment placed inside a case and attached to the right side of entryway doorframes where Jews reside. Written on the scroll are various sections from the Torah, such as the [Shema](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/shema?tab=sources), that feature some of Judaism's central principles.
description.he: המזוזה היא נייר קלף קטן הנמצא בתוך נרתיק (בית המזוזה) המחובר לצד הימני של משקוף הדלת בבתי יהודים. על מגילת הקלף כתובים מגוון קטעים מן התורה, דוגמת פרשת שמע הכוללת כמה מהעקרונות העיקריים של היהדות.

description.en: From the opening narrative of the Torah, when Adam and Eve eat fruit from the tree of knowledge, fruit plays a role in many of the Bible's stories and laws. The spies who scout out the land of Canaan return with massive fruit as an exhibit of the land's qualities, the people of Israel are commanded to bring their first fruit ([*bikkurim*](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/bikkurim)) as an offering to the Temple, and prophets [make](https://www.sefaria.org/Micah.4.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) [use](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.5.2?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) of fruit and fruit trees as metaphors for peace, abundance, and more. Rabbinic literature expands on such instances, analyzing blessings to be said over different fruit and agriculture laws that apply to fruit trees. Later mystical texts delve into the symbolism of fruit, as seen in the [Tu Bishvat Seder](https://www.sefaria.org/Peri_Etz_Hadar?tab=contents), where different fruits correspond to spiritual realms.
description.he: לפירות תפקיד חשוב ביהדות: מהפרי האסור בגן עדן ועד לשבעת המינים, בהם גפן, תאנה ורימון, שעל פי מצוות ביכורים יש להביא את הפרי הראשון שלהם לבית המקדש בירושלים.

description.en: The destruction of the Temple can refer to the destruction of either of the two Temples that stood in Jerusalem in the ancient period. The First Temple, built by King Solomon, as described in the book of I Kings, was destroyed in 586 BCE by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. The Second Temple, built approximately 70 years after the destruction of the first, was destroyed in 70 CE by the Roman Empire.
description.he: חורבן בית המקדש, או בקיצור ״חורבן הבית״, הוא מושג המתייחס לשני אירועים היסטוריים - חורבן בית המקדש הראשון בשנת 586 לפני הספירה על ידי נבוכדנצר מלך בבל, וחורבן בית המקדש השני בשנת 70 לספירה על ידי טיטוס - קיסר האימפריה הרומית. לעיתים, המושג ״חורבן הבית״ מתייחס באופן נרחב יותר לאיבוד עצמאותו המדינית של עם ישראל בארצו בתקופות אלו. בעקבות החורבן, תיקנו חז״ל 4 ימי תענית: עשרה בטבת - בו התחיל המצור על ירושלים בבית ראשון, י״ז בתמוז - יום ביקוע חומות ירושלים, תשעה באב - הצום העיקרי בו חרבו שני בתי המקדש וצום גדליה - בו נרצח גדליה בן אחיקם אשר היה הנציב היהודי בירושלים לאחר חורבן בית ראשון.

description.en: Shemini Atzeret is an early fall holiday that marks the end of the harvest and the start of the rainy season. It directly follows the holiday of [Sukkot](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/sukkot?sort=Relevance&tab=sources) and is observed with prayers for rain in Israel.
description.he: שמיני עצרת הוא חג מקראי שמועדו בכ"ב בתשרי, בסיום חג הסוכות, המציין את סוף הקציר ותחילת עונת הגשמים. בחג זה נאמרים תפילות ופיוטי גשם. בארץ ישראל באותו יום בו חל 'שמיני עצרת' נחגג גם חג 'שמחת תורה', ובחוץ לארץ, חוגגים את 'שמחת תורה' ביום טוב שני של 'שמיני עצרת'.
